summary: Policy types shall include leave, attendance, shift, overtime, pay, expense, loan, benefits and performance; new types shall be definable. (S)
Policies shall be assigned by attribute rules (entity, location, grade, employee type, department, custom field) with precedence and effective dates.
A policy resolution view shall show which policy applies to an employee and why, including the rule and layer responsible.
A country pack shall contain holidays, leave statutes, working-time limits, statutory deductions, tax tables, forms, reports and field requirements.
Pack updates shall be staged: preview which employees' results would change, approve, and activate on an effective date.
Tenants shall override any pack value; overrides survive pack updates and are listed in a diff view.
Policy changes shall be simulated against sample or current employees before activation and shall use the kernel rules engine for conditions and formulas. (new)

The module shall maintain an employee master with personal, contact, address, family and dependents, emergency contacts, education, experience, skills, languages and certifications; all sections configurable per tenant.

The module shall maintain an employment record: employee type (permanent, contract, probation, intern, daily wage, consultant, part-time), status, grade, position, manager, cost center, location, joining date, confirmation date and expected end date.
Every change to employment data shall be effective-dated with a reason code (hire, promotion, transfer, demotion, grade change, acting charge, secondment, rehire, termination).
Employee IDs shall be generated from configurable patterns per entity through kernel numbering, with manual override permission.

National identifiers shall be captured with country-pack validation: Pakistan (CNIC 13 digits with format check and expiry, NTN, EOBI number, social security number, domicile), Saudi Arabia (national ID or iqama, GOSI number, nationality, sponsor), United States (SSN encrypted and masked, work authorization); duplicate identifiers within a tenant shall be flagged.

Bank accounts per employee shall support multiple accounts, IBAN validation, split salary by percentage or amount, effective dates, and maker-checker on changes (aligned with kernel rules for partner bank accounts).
HR shall create employees individually, by bulk import, or by conversion from an accepted offer (wave B).
Employees shall submit data change requests through self-service; changes route through configurable workflow and apply on approval.
Contract management shall cover start and end dates, renewal reminders and workflow, contract history and letters.
Probation tracking shall follow policy: period, extension, early confirmation, reminders to manager and HR.
The profile shall show a timeline of all changes, filterable by type, with an as-of date view.
Bulk update shall change a field across a selected set with preview, approval and rollback.
An employee shall be able to hold multiple concurrent assignments (for example two entities) with a primary flag. (S)
Photo, ID card data and QR code generation shall be supported for ID cards. (S)

The model shall separate Person (one per human, with a person ID) from Employment (one or more per person), so rehires, concurrent engagements and former employees link to one person without duplicate records. (new)
Identifier types, their validation and visibility shall be configurable per country through packs and custom fields rather than fixed columns. (new)
Employees shall optionally link to a kernel user; linking, unlinking and automatic deprovisioning on termination shall be configurable. (new)
Duplicate detection on create and import shall match by identifier, name and date of birth, and bank account blind index, with a review queue and merge audit. (new)
Employee data shall be exportable by the employee in a portable format on request, subject to approval rules. (new, S)
The tenant shall choose a model per entity: position-based (each employee fills a position) or headcount-based (budget per unit and job).
Positions shall carry title, grade, unit, reporting position, location, cost center reference, budgeted FTE, status (planned, open, filled, frozen, closed) and effective dates.
The module shall report sanctioned, filled and vacant strength per unit, grade and location.
An interactive organization chart shall display reporting lines with filters, search, zoom, print and export, including as-of and future-dated views.
A restructure tool shall stage multiple changes (move, merge, split, reassign) as a draft, show impact, and publish atomically on an effective date.
Grades and bands shall define pay ranges, leave entitlements and policy defaults used by the policy framework.
A job catalogue shall store descriptions, responsibilities, qualifications and competencies, versioned.

Organization units used by HRMIS shall be the kernel's units; restructures shall be coordinated so a unit change updates positions, employees and approvers consistently, and notify Finance of cost center mapping changes through events. (new)
When Finance is licensed, headcount cost plans shall be comparable to budgets by cost center. (new, S, wave B)
The document vault shall hold files per employee with categories, document types, issue and expiry dates, and access rules by role.
HR shall request documents from employees with due dates; employees upload through self-service; HR verifies or rejects with reason.
Expiring documents (national ID, visa, residence permit, licenses, certifications) shall trigger notifications at configurable intervals.

Letters shall be generated from templates (offer, appointment, confirmation, increment, promotion, transfer, warning, show-cause, experience, salary certificate, NOC, resignation acceptance, relieving) with merge fields from any object, in the employee's language.
Letters shall pass through an optional approval workflow, then be issued, stored, emailed and acknowledged by the employee.
Policy documents shall be published to selected populations with versioning and acknowledgement tracking.
Employees shall request letters (for example salary certificate) through self-service with automatic generation where the template allows.
Salary-bearing letters and documents shall be generated only by roles with salary permission and shall be logged in the access log. (new)
Attendance shall be captured from web and mobile check-in and check-out, geo-fence validation, selfie capture, QR code, kiosk mode, biometric devices
A device management console shall register devices by site, store connection settings, monitor online status, and show last sync time and errors.

Biometric integration shall support push and pull sync, offline buffering, duplicate removal and mapping of device user IDs to employees; a driver interface shall allow adding device models without core changes.

Mobile capture shall work offline, store punches locally with device time and location, and sync when connected, with tamper checks , follows the offline rules of section 12D, keeps capture time distinct from server receipt time, and is validated by the server after synchronization)
Geo-fences shall be defined per site with radius or polygon and assigned to employees or groups; out-of-fence punches shall be flagged or blocked per policy.
Shift types shall include fixed, flexible (core hours), rotating, split, night and continuous 24-hour; weekly-off patterns shall be configurable (fixed day, rotating, alternating weeks).
A roster builder shall assign shifts to employees or groups for a period, with copy-forward, conflict and rest-hour checks, and publication to employees.
Employees shall request shift swaps and changes through a workflow. (S)
An attendance policy shall define grace periods, late and early-leaving thresholds, half-day and absence thresholds, break and lunch handling, minimum hours for a full day, and rounding rules.
The engine shall process raw punches into daily attendance records (present, absent, late, half-day, on leave, holiday, weekly off, on duty) with an explanation of each result.
Missing or incorrect punches shall appear in an exception queue; employees raise regularization requests with reason and proof; managers approve.

Overtime rules shall be defined by day type (working day, rest day, holiday), with configurable rate multipliers, daily and monthly caps, pre-approval or post-approval, and an option to convert to compensatory off.
Late-coming and early-leaving rules shall support automatic deduction as leave, pay deduction or warning, with waiver by an approver.
On-duty, official visit, work-from-home and field-duty requests shall be supported with approvals and count as present per policy.
Holiday calendars shall be defined per entity and location with Gregorian and Hijri dates, optional holidays and employee choice of optional holidays.
Ramzan (Ramadan) and seasonal timing policies shall apply by date range and employee group.
Attendance periods shall be lockable by cut-off date; changes after lock require approval and trigger a recalculation flag to payroll.
A live dashboard shall show present, absent, late, on leave and not yet punched, by unit and location.
Standard reports shall include daily and monthly muster, late and early, overtime, absenteeism, punch log, device sync and exception ageing.

Biometric data shall be handled under explicit consent: templates stay on devices or are stored encrypted with a retention period, and employees can request deletion on leaving; collection can be disabled per entity. : this requirement governs biometric attendance devices; biometric unlock of the mobile application uses the operating system's credential and stores no template in HRMIS (section 12E).
Locking an attendance period shall publish an AttendanceLocked event used by payroll, and reopening shall publish AttendanceReopened with the affected employees. (new)
Project, client and task time entry with billable flag, approval and lock shall be available as timesheets (required for United States tenants and professional-services customers). (new, wave B)

basis: One circular office fence in Phase 1 (D-42)
summary: The system shall maintain attendance locations of types office, branch, factory, warehouse, project site, customer premises, construction site, temporary field location and other authorized work location. Attendance locations shall extend the kernel Organization locations; a location shall not be duplicated as a second master record.

basis: One circular office fence in Phase 1 (D-42)
summary: Each attendance location shall carry a name, unique identifier, address, geographical coordinates, status, effective start and end dates, applicable employees or rules, and the authorized administrators.

basis: One circular office fence in Phase 1 (D-42)
summary: Each location shall support one or more geo-fence boundaries: circular

basis: One circular office fence in Phase 1 (D-42)
summary: Radius and boundary values shall be configurable within allowed minimum and maximum limits set by tenant policy; the default radius is a proposal

Applicability shall be assignable to employees, departments, teams, shifts and employee categories by attribute rules with effective dates and precedence, using the kernel data scopes and the policy framework
Employees may hold a primary and secondary attendance locations; a roster line may specify the location for a given day

Temporary field locations shall be creatable by authorized users for a defined period, optionally through an approval workflow, and shall expire automatically; expired locations cannot validate new events.

Locations shall have the lifecycle draft, active, inactive and archived; boundary or applicability changes shall be effective-dated and versioned so past attendance results are never altered by later changes.

A map-based editor shall support address search, placing a point, drawing a circle or polygon, and previewing which employees the location applies to; import of boundaries from standard geographic files shall be available.
Boundary data shall be validated: valid coordinate ranges, minimum radius, no self-intersecting polygons, and warnings for overlapping geo-fences of different locations.
Every change to a location, geo-fence or assignment shall be audited with before and after values and the acting user; managing geo-fences shall require its own permission
Bulk import, export and bulk assignment of locations and applicability shall be supported with validation and preview.
The system shall provide four configurable location policy modes, set per organization, employee category, department, location and other policy dimensions with precedence and effective dates

Mode A: attendance shall be accepted only when the verified device location falls inside an authorized geo-fence under the accuracy rule; otherwise the submission shall be rejected with a clear reason and the employee may submit a regularization request where policy allows.

Mode B: attendance outside the geo-fence shall be accepted as a submission, the actual coordinates captured, the distance from the assigned location recorded, the record flagged as an exception, the employee's reason captured, and the record routed for review by policy.
Mode C: attendance may be recorded from any location; coordinates shall be captured and be available to authorized supervisors and HR; no geo-fence rejection applies.
Mode D: employees with a field-duty assignment
Policy parameters shall include: accuracy threshold
The policy resolution view of POL-03 shall explain which mode applies to an employee on a date and why.
Policy changes shall be effective-dated and simulated against recent events to show which results would change before activation

Before an employee's first location-bearing capture, the application shall show the purpose notice for location capture and record the acknowledgement, in the employee's language, configurable per country
Employees approved to work remotely shall be assigned Mode B or C; home coordinates shall not be stored unless the tenant explicitly configures it
Event types shall include check-in, check-out, break start, break end and other configured types.

For each applicable event the system shall capture: employee ID; event type; event timestamp; server receipt timestamp; device timestamp; GPS latitude and longitude; GPS accuracy where available; resolved address or location description where available; assigned workplace or geo-fence; distance from the authorized location; geo-fence validation result; device identifier and registration reference; application and platform information; network status at capture; validation and exception flags; employee reason where applicable; approval or regularization status.
The event timestamp
Device clock tampering shall be detected by comparing device and server time at connection and by monotonic-clock offsets; events with skew above a threshold

The geo-fence validation result shall use defined codes: inside, outside, accuracy insufficient, location unavailable, location services disabled, mock suspected, unverified offline, unrecognized location.
Reverse geocoding shall be optional and informational, through a configurable provider adapter
Duplicate prevention shall use an idempotency key per event and a duplicate window; sequence rules
A photograph shall be optional by policy and stored as evidence with its own retention; automated face matching is not provided
Raw location evidence shall be stored separately from the attendance result
Accepted events are immutable; corrections occur through regularization with full history, never by editing the captured event.

Configurable exception types shall include: outside geo-fence; GPS unavailable; poor GPS accuracy; location services disabled; mock or suspicious location; missing check-in or check-out; duplicate events; late arrival and early departure; offline synchronization; unrecognized or unauthorized location; attendance at an incorrect work location. Each type has severity, routing and optional auto-resolution rules.
Where policy permits, employees shall submit explanations and regularization requests with reason and attachments within a time limit, through the mobile app or web.
Supervisors, managers and HR shall review, approve, reject or return exceptions for correction according to their authority, determined by data scope and by thresholds
Reminders and escalation to the next approver shall follow configurable timing; automatic approval is not a default
A complete, immutable decision history shall record who decided, when, comments, and previous and new values.
Regularization shall change the attendance outcome only; the original captured event and its evidence remain unchanged.
Reviewers shall have bulk tools with filters and grouping by location, team and exception type, and one-tap actions on mobile.
Repeated exceptions by an employee or at a location shall be surfaced to HR as advisory indicators; no disciplinary or pay action shall be triggered automatically
Employees shall see their own exceptions, status and decisions, with notifications.
Unresolved exceptions shall be shown to payroll at attendance lock
Mock or suspicious location indicators
Distance and severity thresholds for routing shall be configurable by policy.

A live dashboard shall show employees present, absent, late, on leave, working remotely, on field duty, with attendance exceptions and pending approvals, with distribution by location, department, branch and organization, limited to the viewer's data scope.
Dashboard data shall be near real time
An interactive map shall show attendance event markers

Selecting a marker shall show event details: recorded GPS position, assigned workplace, inside or outside, distance, device and application information, evidence photo where permitted, and exception state.
Users shall drill down to an employee's attendance history and see the event points of a chosen period; the map shows event points only, never a continuous trail.
Map and evidence visibility shall respect the viewer's data scope and a separate permission to view GPS evidence; users without it see only inside or outside and the exception status.
Map and dashboard queries shall use the semantic layer with query limits, and exporting coordinates shall follow export controls and approval
Continuous, real-time movement tracking of individuals between events is not provided and is Won't have in this release; any safety-motivated exception
The dashboard and map shall be available on web and mobile workspaces
Executive map access shall be configurable and disabled unless the tenant policy enables it for senior management
Retention of raw location evidence shall be configurable per tenant and entity and independent of the retention of attendance results; the default is a proposal
Every view or export of location evidence shall be written to the access log with user, scope and purpose where required.
Employees shall be able to see their own recorded events and locations and the location notice.
Precision shall be reducible by policy
Aggregated analytics shall be preferred to individual-level location data where the purpose does not need individuals.
An entity or country flag shall disable location capture entirely; events then record time and device information only.
Authorized users shall create individual tasks with title, description, instructions and expected deliverables.
A task shall be assignable to one employee, several employees, a team or a department; assignment to a team or department creates one assignment per member at the time of assignment.
A task shall carry priority, start date, due date, expected duration, assigned supervisor or reviewer, and an optional association with a project
A task shall define whether location capture is required and at which events
Reference documents and instructions shall be attachable and shown to assignees.
Tasks may depend on other tasks
Task types shall be configurable
Task templates shall store type, instructions, checkpoints, evidence and review rules for reuse; recurring task definitions shall generate tasks on a schedule with assignment rules.
A user may assign tasks only to employees within their data scope; assignment outside the scope requires a specific permission and is audited.
When assigning, the system shall warn about conflicts with approved leave, rest days and shift hours of the assignee, and about workload above a configured limit.
For multiple assignees the task shall define a completion mode: each assignee completes and is reviewed separately
Bulk assignment and import of tasks from a spreadsheet shall be supported with validation and preview.
Assignment shall notify assignees and reviewers through the notification service
Reassignment of an open task shall be possible by the assigner or manager with reason, keeping history.
The task lifecycle shall have ten statuses: Draft, Assigned, Acknowledged, In Progress, On Hold, Submitted for Review, Returned for Rework, Completed or Approved, Rejected, and Cancelled or Closed
Valid transitions, permitted actors and conditions shall be as in the table below and enforced by the status model
Every status change shall record actor, time, reason
An unacknowledged task shall trigger reminders and escalation after a configurable period.
Submission for review shall be blocked until required checkpoints, evidence and mandatory fields are complete.
The number of rework cycles shall be recorded and a configurable limit may escalate the task to the next reviewer.
Completed tasks shall close automatically after a configurable period and may be reopened by an authorized manager with a reason.
Overdue status shall be derived from due date and status, not stored as a separate status, and shall drive reminders and reports.
When an assignee leaves the organization or becomes inactive, open tasks shall be flagged for reassignment
Review and approval of submissions shall use the kernel workflow engine so reviewer resolution, delegation, escalation and out-of-office rules apply.
Employees shall see their assigned tasks
Employees shall review instructions, deadlines and reference documents and acknowledge the assignment.
Employees shall start a task and submit progress updates with comments.
Employees shall record work performed
Employees shall attach photographs, documents and, where configured, a recipient signature as evidence, with size and type limits and compression on mobile.
Employees shall complete required checkpoints in the configured order or freely, each with optional location and evidence.
Employees shall submit the task for review with completion details.
Employees shall respond to reviewer feedback, add comments and resubmit after rework.
Employees shall view the history and status of their tasks.
All employee actions shall work offline within the rules of section 12D, with queued submissions and clear status.
Employees shall be told before location is captured for a task event and shall see which events capture location.
Employees shall be able to report that a task cannot be performed with a reason from a configured list, which routes to the assigner.

Location capture shall be configurable per task type and per task at these events: task start, progress update, checkpoint completion, task submission, and other configured field activity events. The default for a task type without a location policy is no location capture.
The system shall not assume every task requires GPS.

For each location-enabled event the system shall capture: employee ID; task ID; event type; event timestamp; server receipt timestamp; GPS latitude and longitude; GPS accuracy; resolved address where available; device and application information; location validation status; and associated photograph or document evidence.
A task may specify an assigned location
Policy shall define whether an out-of-area event is blocked, accepted with a flag and reason, or accepted without validation; the default is accepted with a flag and reason.
Mock-location signals and device risk signals shall be flagged as for attendance
Events captured offline shall keep capture time and server receipt time and shall be validated by the server after synchronization
Location evidence of tasks follows the retention, access and audit rules of ATT-77 to ATT-82 and section 34, with the task evidence retention proposal in MD-09.
Supervisors, managers, department heads and authorized senior management shall see assigned tasks, employee responses, progress and completion status within their data scope.
Reviewers shall view submitted photographs, documents and checklist answers.
Authorized users shall see task event locations on an interactive map and compare them to the assigned location or geo-fence, with inside or outside and distance.
Reviewers shall approve, reject or return task submissions with comments and instructions through the workflow engine, from web or mobile.
Users shall see an employee's activity history for tasks within their scope.
Overdue and delayed tasks shall be highlighted with reminders to assignees and escalations to supervisors.
Team and departmental task performance shall be shown on dashboards
Map visibility shall respect role, data scope and the separate permission to view GPS evidence; users without it see only validation results.
Comments between reviewer and assignee shall use kernel collaboration comments with the task's visibility rules.
Senior management map views shall be disabled unless the tenant policy enables them

Reports and dashboards shall cover: tasks assigned by employee, team, department and manager; completed; pending; overdue; average completion time; rejected and returned; employee task activity; field activity by geographical area; performance by department and location; completion trends; and supervisor review and approval turnaround.
GPS presence and the number of task events shall not be presented as productivity; productivity indicators shall be configurable, explainable business measures
Individual-level task analytics shall be restricted to the employee, their reporting line and authorized HR; aggregated views shall be the default for senior management.
Reports shall use the kernel semantic layer, respect data scopes and privacy controls, and be exportable under export controls.
Predictive or ranking features based on task or location data are Won't have in this release; any future use requires bias and privacy review
Task data shall be available to the AI assistant only within the requesting user's permissions and shall not drive automated performance, pay or disciplinary decisions
Notifications shall cover assignment, acknowledgement reminders, deadline reminders, overdue alerts, review comments, approval, rejection and rework.
All task and evidence actions, including views of location and evidence, shall be audited.
Evidence retention periods shall be configurable per task type and entity, with a default proposal
Photographs shall be scanned, compressed and stored encrypted; embedded location metadata of images shall be handled according to policy
Task custom fields, labels and checklists shall be configurable through the kernel metadata engine without code.
Task types and templates shall be exportable and importable as configuration packages.
Tasks shall be searchable by title, assignee, status and location within the user's scope.
The employee shall be able to see which fields and events a supervisor can see for their tasks.
Task assignment across legal entities requires explicit permission and respects entity-level policies.
The module shall expose its task events to integrations through the integration framework

Leave types shall be unlimited and configurable (annual, casual, sick, maternity, paternity, marriage, Hajj, Umrah, bereavement, study, unpaid, compensatory off and custom), each with paid or unpaid flag, calendar or working-day counting and document requirement.

Entitlement models shall include fixed yearly grant, monthly accrual, accrual per days or hours worked, tenure-based tiers, grade-based tiers and manual grant, with configurable pro-rata for joiners and leavers.

Rules per leave type shall include carry-forward with cap and expiry, encashment with cap and rate basis, negative balance allowance, minimum notice, maximum consecutive days, gender and tenure eligibility, probation eligibility, sandwich rules for holiday and weekend adjacency, and combining restrictions.
Employees shall apply for full-day, half-day and hourly leave with attachments and see the balance impact before submitting.
Requests shall route through the kernel workflow engine; managers see the team calendar and coverage warnings; HR can apply leave on behalf of an employee.
Cancellation and modification of approved leave shall be supported, with approvals where policy requires and automatic balance restoration.
Leave without pay shall flow to payroll as an attendance-based deduction (wave A2).
Compensatory off shall be earned from approved overtime or holiday work, with expiry rules.
Blackout periods and maximum concurrent leave by team shall be configurable.
A leave ledger per employee shall show opening balance, accruals, usage, adjustments, encashment, lapse and closing balance with source documents.
Year-end processing shall carry forward, lapse and encash per policy, with preview and rollback until confirmed.

Country packs shall preload statutory leave minimums and special leave (for example maternity and paternity provisions in Pakistan, Hajj leave and statutory leave in Saudi Arabia) as editable defaults.
A leave liability calculation (days and value by employee and entity) shall be produced each period and, when Finance is licensed, published for accrual posting by posting rules. (new, wave A2)
Leave balances and entitlements shall be recomputable from the ledger and policies for audit, and every recomputation shall explain differences. (new)
Managers shall see team leave calendars and availability
Employees shall be able to add supporting documents when applying, including photographs from the mobile camera, with type and size limits and scanning.
Managers shall approve or reject leave with comments from the mobile workspace using the same workflow, rules and authority as on the web
Onboarding checklists shall be built per employee type, entity, location or role with tasks, owners (HR, IT, admin, manager, employee), due dates relative to joining date, and reminders.
A pre-boarding portal shall let the new hire complete forms, upload documents, accept policies and provide bank details before day one.
Resignation shall be submitted by the employee or recorded by HR, with notice period determined by policy, acceptance workflow and last working day calculation.
Offboarding checklists shall include clearance by department, asset return, access removal and knowledge handover, with outstanding items shown to payroll for final settlement.
Exit interviews shall use configurable forms visible only to authorized HR roles.
Termination types (resignation, termination, end of contract, retirement, death, absconding) shall carry different workflows and letters.
Onboarding shall include buddy assignment, 30-60-90 day plans, scheduled check-ins and new-hire surveys.
Provisioning tasks shall call integrations (email account, directory, ticketing) to create or disable accounts automatically. (S)
Probation reviews shall be configured as forms with manager and HR sign-off, producing confirmation, extension or termination outcomes.
Offboarding shall capture exit reasons in a standard taxonomy for attrition analysis, and keep alumni records with rehire eligibility flags.
Employees shall submit a resignation, see its status and notice period, and receive the acceptance decision on mobile and web.
Employees and clearance owners shall see and complete their exit checklist and handover tasks on mobile, with evidence where required.
Exit interview scheduling and, where configured, completion of the exit form shall be available on mobile; responses remain visible only to authorized HR roles
Employees shall see the status of the final settlement and their separation documents; settlement amounts are shown only to the employee and authorized HR and payroll roles.

The employee portal shall provide profile, documents, payslips and tax documents (wave A2), attendance, leave, requests and their status, letters, directory, organization chart, announcements and policies.
The manager portal shall provide an approvals inbox (kernel workflow inbox), team dashboard (attendance, leave, birthdays, probation and contract dates), team calendar and request-on-behalf actions.
HR and payroll workspaces shall provide task queues, exceptions, deadlines and quick actions.
Mobile apps shall provide attendance capture, leave and request submission, approvals, payslips, directory and push notifications, with biometric unlock.
Chat-based self-service through WhatsApp shall support leave balance, leave application, attendance summary and payslip request, authenticated by registered number and a one-time code. (S)
Tenants shall configure home page widgets, quick links, welcome content and language defaults per role.
Employees and managers shall set delegation and out-of-office from self-service, applied to approvals through the kernel delegation feature. (new)
Self-service shall be available in English, Urdu and Arabic with right-to-left layout and Hijri date display. (new)
The web portal and the mobile applications shall be clients of the same HRMIS services; a function offered on both shall behave identically, with the same validation, workflow and authorization
Availability of each self-service function per client
Home widgets shall be role-aware and configurable per role and tenant on web and mobile
Profile change requests, HR service requests and document requests shall be available on both clients through the same workflows
Self-service actions started offline on mobile shall follow the offline rules of section 12D and shall never bypass server-side validation or approval.
Self-service on both clients shall meet the accessibility, localization and performance rules of document 13.
The mobile application shall be delivered Android first
The mobile application is a client of the HRMIS platform and not a separate HR system: it shall hold no business rules that are not enforced by the server and shall not own master data.
Functionality shall be consistent across Android and iOS, subject to platform-specific capabilities
The mobile architecture shall allow reuse of mobile UI components and logic across platforms where technically appropriate.
The application shall run on lower-end Android devices within the performance budgets of document 13
The application shall be distributable through the channels chosen by decision MD-02
The application shall expose only functions of licensed modules and enabled tenant features
Minimum supported application versions shall be enforceable by the server, with update prompts and backward-compatible APIs for the previous version
The assistant of AIA-01 to AIA-05 shall be available inside the application when enabled, within the same permissions and safety rules.
Tenant branding

The application shall provide experiences for the roles Employee, Manager, Supervisor, Department Head, HR Administrator, HR Business Partner, Regional Manager, Senior Management, and other configurable roles, selected from the user's Kernel roles and data scopes.
Mobile permissions shall equal web permissions: a user with several roles sees the union of functions allowed by those roles, and nothing more because they use a mobile device.
Role-specific workspaces shall be exposed as additional areas of the same application
Role and data scope changes shall take effect on the next request or sync without reinstalling or re-registering the application.
Sign-in shall support employee ID, username or email according to tenant configuration, and password authentication.
Single sign-on shall be supported where the tenant configures an identity provider
Multi-factor authentication shall be supported, including one-time codes by authenticator, SMS or email according to tenant policy, with enforcement by role or user

Biometric unlock shall use device-supported authentication to unlock an application session that was already authenticated by the server; it shall not replace server-side authentication or authorization, and HRMIS shall not store biometric templates. Policy
Each device shall be registered securely on first sign-in with a device identifier, platform, application version and user binding; a user's registered devices are limited by policy
Trusted-device policies shall determine which devices may access which functions; unrecognized devices shall require additional verification or administrator approval according to policy.
Session timeout, inactivity lock and session revocation shall be configurable; tokens shall be device-bound and rotate on use
Password reset and account recovery shall be available through verified channels without revealing whether an account exists.
Authorized administrators shall revoke a device or remotely sign out a user, wipe locally stored application data on the next connection, and see the revocation in the audit log.
Configurable limits for failed sign-ins and suspicious sign-in patterns

The home screen shall be role-aware and configurable and shall show relevant widgets from: today's attendance status, check-in and check-out actions, assigned shift, attendance exceptions, leave balance, upcoming holidays, pending leave requests, assigned tasks, task deadlines, pending approvals
Widgets shall appear only for functions the user may use and modules licensed
Tenants shall configure widget availability and order per role; users may reorder within allowed limits.
The home screen shall load from cached data immediately and refresh in the background, showing data freshness.
Primary daily actions
Employees shall check in, check out, and start and end breaks under the location policy mode that applies to them
The application shall show attendance history, a daily summary and a monthly calendar view, the assigned shift, and overtime information where applicable.
Employees shall submit regularization requests, missing attendance submissions and exception explanations with attachments where policy permits
Field-duty employees shall record attendance at approved field locations or other permitted locations under Mode D
Before capture the application shall check location permission and service state, guide the employee to enable them, and explain the purpose notice
The application shall show geo-fence feedback: distance from the assigned location, whether inside or outside, and the accuracy reached.
After each submission the application shall show a clear status: accepted, rejected with reason, or submitted for review; and for offline captures, locally captured and not yet accepted by the server
Offline attendance capture and synchronization shall follow section 12D and the per-mode permission of MD-08.
Employees shall view leave balances, leave types and applicable policies, leave history and the organizational holiday calendar.
Employees shall apply for leave with dates, duration, reason and supporting documents, see the balance effect before submitting, and cancel or amend applications where policy permits.
Employees shall track application status and see approval or rejection comments, with notifications.
Managers shall review team leave requests and team availability within their data scope

Employees shall view personal details, contact information, employment information, job title and designation, department and reporting manager, work location, emergency contacts, qualifications and skills, employment documents and profile photograph, within field security.
Bank details shall be shown only where permitted, masked by default, with reveal protected by step-up authentication and logged.
Employees shall submit profile change requests; sensitive changes
Profile photographs shall be captured or chosen with size and quality checks and routed for approval where policy requires.

Employees shall access authorized documents: employment and appointment letters, contracts, salary certificates, payslips, tax documents, policy documents, performance documents and training certificates, and other employee-specific documents.
Secure viewing and downloading shall follow document permissions, retention rules and tenant policy; downloads of sensitive types may be disabled or watermarked.
Sensitive documents shall not be cached on the device unless the tenant allows it, in which case they are encrypted and removed on sign-out or revocation.
Employees shall request letters and certificates and upload requested documents

Employees shall view monthly payslips, salary history, earnings and deductions, allowances, bonuses and incentives, tax deductions, loans and advances, reimbursements and expenses, year-to-date information, and tax statements and certificates where applicable.

Access to payroll screens shall be restricted by role and field security, may require step-up authentication, and shall mask amounts when the screen is idle or when the app is in the background, according to policy.
Payslip availability shall be notified without including amounts in the notification.
Employees shall submit expense claims and loan requests from mobile where those modules are enabled

Employees shall view, acknowledge, start and update tasks, record progress and checkpoints, upload photographs and supporting evidence, submit completion reports, respond to review comments, resubmit and view their task history
Location shall be captured at the configured task events only, with the notice of TFA-35 and the offline behavior of section 12D.
A map view shall show location-enabled tasks and the employee's own recorded event points where appropriate.
The camera flow shall support multiple photographs per task event, compression, retake and caption, within the limits of the task type.

Employees shall submit and track requests in configurable categories including general HR inquiries, employment verification, salary certificate, documents, payroll queries, attendance complaints, leave queries, profile corrections, and integrated IT or administrative requests.
Requests shall allow attachments, show status and responses, and notify the employee at each step.
Requests shall use the kernel workflow and service-request facilities and the helpdesk of ERL-05 where licensed; no separate request engine shall be built.
Employees shall view internal job opportunities, apply internally, follow application status, refer candidates and receive related communications.
The feature shall use the recruitment module's postings, applications and notifications; no separate recruitment store shall be created.
Employees shall see assigned training, schedules, course details, learning materials, progress, completion status and certificates, and receive training reminders.
Employees shall view objectives and key indicators, review schedules, complete self-assessment, give and receive feedback, see review status and development plans, and track goals and progress.
Managers shall complete authorized reviews and feedback from their mobile workspace.
The application shall show company announcements, HR notices, policy updates and circulars, with acknowledgement tracking where required
An employee directory shall be shown according to privacy settings

Employees shall submit resignation, see its status, follow the exit checklist and clearance tasks, schedule the exit interview, see handover requirements, final settlement status and separation documents, as specified in ONB-14 to ONB-17, with access to sensitive settlement information limited to authorized roles.
Managers and supervisors shall see their direct reports and, according to scope, the wider team, with current status
They shall see authorized team attendance, late arrivals and absences for the day and period, and review attendance exceptions and regularization requests
They shall approve or reject leave applications and see team leave calendars and availability
They shall create and assign tasks within their data scope, review progress and submissions, view task-related evidence and location results, and approve, reject or return task submissions
They shall add comments and instructions on tasks and exceptions and receive reminders for pending approvals.
A single approvals inbox shall list pending decisions across modules
Bulk approval shall be available where policy permits, with a confirmation that states the number of items.
Delegation and out-of-office settings
A team dashboard shall show attendance, leave, task status, overdue tasks, probation and contract dates.
Employee contact details shall be shown only as allowed by privacy settings; calling or messaging a team member from the application shall use the device's own facilities.
Reports to the manager shall be limited to their own team unless a wider scope is granted.
Authorized HR users shall view employee information within their assigned scope and field security.
They shall review attendance exceptions and regularization requests and leave requests assigned to HR.
They shall monitor employee requests and HR helpdesk cases, with ageing and service levels.
They shall see workforce dashboards for their scope
They shall review task and field activity information where authorized, without evidence or location unless the GPS evidence permission is held
They shall monitor and decide employee data change requests, with verification steps for sensitive fields.
They shall receive workflow alerts and escalations for items past their service levels.

HR users shall see whether an employee has a registered device and the application version, for support purposes, without access to the employee's location history; revoking a device requires the device management permission
HR Business Partners shall see only the units assigned to them.

An executive dashboard shall show configurable high-level indicators: total headcount; active and inactive employees; attendance overview; absenteeism and late arrivals; leave utilization; workforce distribution; departmental headcount; task completion and overdue tasks; field workforce activity; workforce trends; and other approved HR indicators.
Indicators shall be aggregated by default, with drill-down to departments, locations and, only where authorized, individuals.
Regional managers shall see their regions; senior management shall see the scopes granted to their roles; comparisons across departments and regions shall be available within scope.
Map views for senior management shall be controlled by permission and by the tenant's location privacy policy, and shall show aggregated or event-level data as configured
Executive indicator definitions shall be shown on demand so the figures are explainable
The last synchronized dashboard shall remain viewable offline with its timestamp, and sensitive drill-downs shall require connection
Compensation figures shall appear only for roles granted salary permission
Narrative summaries of changes may be offered by the AI assistant for review, within permissions
Channels shall be in-app, mobile push, email, SMS and, where an approved integration exists, WhatsApp, each selectable per event type by tenant policy and per user within allowed limits.

Events shall include: attendance reminders; attendance submission accepted or failed; attendance exceptions; leave submission, approval and rejection; task assignment, deadline reminders, review comments, approval and rejection; pending manager approvals; HR service-request updates; payslip availability; company announcements; policy updates; and security alerts.
Templates shall be configurable per event, channel and language
Users shall set preferences by event group and channel and quiet hours, except for mandatory notifications such as security alerts.
Delivery status
Push and message content shall not include sensitive data such as salary amounts, location coordinates or settlement figures; details are shown after authentication.
Notifications shall carry deep links that open the relevant screen with the user's permissions checked.
Third-party providers shall be reached only through the kernel's provider adapters; no provider shall be referenced in HRMIS business logic
A notification center in the application shall list notifications with read state, retention and search.
Reminders
Escalation notifications shall follow workflow escalation rules
Rate limits and deduplication shall prevent notification floods; digests shall be available for noisy events.
Critical announcements and policy updates may require acknowledgement and shall track it
Notifications shall be localized to the recipient's language, calendar and number formats.
The device token lifecycle
All notifications that carry decisions or deadlines shall be written to the audit trail with time and delivery result.
The application shall define, per feature and per tenant policy, whether it works offline, and shall show the user clearly which actions are available without a connection.
Local data shall be limited to what the user needs, stored in an encrypted local database and encrypted files, with keys bound to the user's session and device
Pending actions shall be held in an offline event queue with idempotency keys, capture timestamp, device timestamp, location and evidence references, and be sent when connectivity returns.

The server shall validate every queued event on receipt against the policies, authority and data scope effective at the capture time, and may accept, reject or route it to review; offline capture never implies acceptance.
The application shall distinguish locally captured, uploading, accepted by the server, rejected and in review for every event, and never show a local event as accepted before the server confirms.
Duplicate events shall be prevented by idempotency keys and duplicate windows; replays shall not create new records
Conflicts
Capture time and server receipt time shall be stored separately and shown separately
Failed synchronization shall be retried with back-off, shown in a synchronization status screen with reasons, and escalated to the user after a configurable number of failures.
The user shall see overall synchronization status
A maximum offline period shall be configurable; after it, sensitive cached data is locked until the next successful sync.
On sign-out, device revocation, deprovisioning or a wipe command, locally stored data shall be erased, and unsynchronized events shall be handled by policy
Offline photographs and attachments shall be size limited, compressed and retried as chunks, with progress and retry controls.
Device clock changes made while offline shall be detected on reconnection and flagged
Selective synchronization limits
Offline behavior shall be covered by tests that simulate loss and return of connectivity, interrupted uploads and device restarts.
All API traffic shall use TLS with certificate validation; certificate pinning shall be available as a tenant option.
Tokens and secrets shall be kept in the operating system's secure storage; no credentials shall be stored in plain files or logs.
The local database and cached files shall be encrypted; keys shall be protected by device secure hardware where available.
Device registration, trust state, session expiry, revocation, remote logout and data wipe shall work as in MOB-24 to MOB-28 and be audited.
Rooted Android and jailbroken iOS devices shall be detected through device risk signals
Mock-location and location manipulation shall be detected where technically feasible and handled as signals for review
Application integrity controls
APIs shall be protected by rate limiting, abuse detection and authorization checks on every request; the client is never trusted for authorization.
Sensitive data
Sensitive screens shall hide content in the task switcher and may block screenshots and screen recording according to tenant policy.
Clipboard use of sensitive values shall be restricted by policy.
Secure document access shall follow FR-HRM-MOB-70 to MOB-72; downloaded files shall be encrypted and removable on sign-out.
Mobile events shall be written to the audit log: sign-in and failures, device registration and revocation, attendance and task captures, location evidence views, exports, and administrative actions.
Device and session policies
The application shall be compatible with enterprise mobile device and application management solutions where the customer requires them
A penetration test and a mobile application security review shall be completed before each major release
Dependencies of the mobile application shall pass the license and vulnerability gates of document 12.

Location and employee activity data shall be collected only for the documented business purposes of section 34; the purposes, the events that trigger capture, the roles that can see it, the retention periods, the employee notice and the audit of access shall be configurable and documented per tenant and country.
Continuous background location tracking is not designed as a default and is Won't have in this release
The primary navigation shall have five destinations: Home, Attendance, Tasks, Leave and Profile. Other features shall be reached from the home dashboard, contextual navigation or a Services menu.
Users with manager, HR or executive roles shall switch between My view and a role workspace
Frequent actions
Navigation items shall appear only for licensed modules, enabled functions and permitted roles
Attendance and task statuses shall use consistent status chips with text and icon, never color alone
Controls shall meet the touch target, contrast and text scaling rules of document 13, work one-handed for primary actions, and support light, dark and high-contrast themes.

The application shall support English, Urdu and Arabic, right-to-left layout for Urdu and Arabic, localized dates, numbers, currencies and times, and Gregorian and Hijri calendars where country policy requires them, all through the shared Kernel localization services.
Validation and error messages shall say what happened and how to fix it, in the user's language, and offline and sync states shall be explained
The application shall be optimized for low bandwidth: small payloads, deferred images, compressed uploads, and a usable offline home.
Notification taps and deep links shall open the exact screen after authentication and permission checks.
Global search within the user's scope shall find people, tasks, requests and documents the user may see
Settings shall include language, notifications, security
Clickable prototypes of attendance, task, approval and executive dashboards shall be tested with representative users, including Urdu and Arabic speakers and field staff, before build
All mobile APIs shall be versioned; the server shall support the current and previous major version of the application API for at least one release
Errors shall use the kernel problem-details model with stable error codes the application can translate; validation errors shall identify fields.
Every write that can be retried shall accept an idempotency key and produce one result for repeated requests
Requests shall carry both the capture time and the device time where relevant; responses shall return the server receipt time and the validation result
Authorization shall be enforced on the server for every request, using the same Kernel permissions and data scopes as the web
Input validation shall be strict
Rate limiting and abuse detection shall apply per user, device and tenant with clear responses and retry hints.
List endpoints shall use cursor pagination and support conditional requests so the application can refresh cheaply.
Synchronization endpoints shall support delta retrieval by scope, resumable upload of queued events and attachments, and per-item results
Audit records shall be written for the operations listed in the table, with correlation identifiers that tie mobile requests to server actions.
Public documentation
Contract tests shall verify the application against the API on every release, including the previous application version.
Logs and traces shall exclude sensitive values
The mobile APIs shall be the same APIs available to other approved clients and integrations, subject to client permissions; no hidden mobile-only business endpoints shall bypass rules.
Dashboards shall include headcount, joiners and leavers, demographics, attrition, attendance, leave liability, and contract and probation expiries.

Standard reports shall include employee master, strength by unit, grade and location, movement report, birthdays and anniversaries, document expiry, leave balance, leave utilization and attendance summaries.
All standard reports shall be cloneable and editable through the report builder.
HR semantic models shall respect data scopes and hide compensation fields unless the user has salary permission. (new)
Attendance and location reports and dashboards listed in section 13A shall be standard content of the module.
Task and field activity reports and dashboards listed in section 13A shall be standard content of the module
Mobile application reports for administrators
Executive reporting listed in section 13A shall be available on web and in the senior management workspace

Reports and maps that use location data shall run through the semantic layer, apply the GPS evidence permission and data scopes, write access to the access log, and follow export controls and approval

Location and task reporting shall be aggregated by default; individual-level views shall be restricted to the employee, their reporting line and authorized HR, and shall never present GPS presence or event counts as productivity
Pay groups shall define frequency (monthly, semi-monthly, bi-weekly, weekly), calendar, cut-off dates, payment dates, currency and entity; an employee belongs to exactly one pay group at a time.

Pay components shall be unlimited and typed as earning, deduction, employer contribution, reimbursement or informational, each with taxable, pensionable, EOBI-able and other statutory-base flags configured by pack.
Component calculation methods shall include fixed amount, percentage of another component, formula, slab or table lookup, per-day or per-hour rate, attendance-linked, and manual input.
Salary structures shall bundle components with order of evaluation, assignable by grade, employee type or individually, effective-dated.
Pro-rata rules (calendar days, working days, fixed 30 days, custom) shall be configurable per component for joiners, leavers, unpaid leave and mid-month changes.
Salary revisions shall record old and new structure, effective date and reason; backdated revisions shall compute arrears automatically over affected periods.

Payroll inputs shall come from locked attendance, leave without pay, overtime, loans and advances, approved expense reimbursements, bonuses, incentives and one-time adjustments, and shall be importable from files.
Bonuses (Eid, annual, performance, ad hoc) shall be defined with eligibility, basis and tax treatment and processed in regular or off-cycle runs.
Payroll shall support holding an employee's salary with reason and releasing it in a later run.
Run stages shall be create, import inputs, calculate, validate, review, approve, lock, generate bank files and payslips, post to accounting, and close; each stage records user and time.
Validation shall flag negative net pay, missing bank data, missing tax IDs, changes above a configurable threshold versus the last run, duplicate payments, and employees without attendance data.
A variance report shall compare current and previous runs by employee and component with drill-down to the cause.
Payroll shall support dual approval (maker-checker) with thresholds by total amount or variance.
A run may be recalculated for a subset of employees; a locked run may be reopened only with elevated permission and an audit reason.
Off-cycle runs (bonus, correction, final settlement, advance) shall be supported without disturbing the regular run.
Retroactive changes discovered after lock shall produce correction entries in the next open run and never overwrite a closed run.

Income tax shall be computed from effective-dated slab tables by tax year (July to June for Pakistan), including rebates and surcharge, using projected annual income with monthly adjustment and year-end true-up.
Tax on bonuses, arrears, leave encashment, gratuity and other irregular payments shall follow configurable treatment (taxed in the month, averaged, or separate rate).
Tax exemptions and credits shall be capturable through employee declarations with proof upload and HR verification.

Statutory contributions shall be calculated from configurable bases and rates (Pakistan: EOBI employee and employer, provincial social security, Workers Welfare Fund, Workers Profit Participation Fund, provident fund, gratuity accrual).
Rates, ceilings and bases shall come from pack tables, overridable per tenant; no statutory rate shall be hard-coded.
Previous-employer income and tax paid shall be captured for mid-year joiners and included in tax computation.
Salary payment files shall be generated per bank format (configurable templates), including bulk and inter-bank formats, validated before download.
Payment modes shall include bank transfer, cheque, cash and mobile wallet, per employee, with split by percentage or amount.
Payment status shall be updatable by import of bank files (paid, failed), with failed payments queued for correction and re-payment.

Final settlement shall compute pending salary, leave encashment, gratuity or end-of-service benefit, notice-period shortfall or payment, loan and advance recovery, asset recovery, bonus and tax adjustment.
Settlement shall depend on offboarding clearance status and produce a settlement statement and a full-and-final letter for acknowledgement.
Payslips shall be generated from designable bilingual templates, delivered as password-protected PDF by email and shown in self-service, with year-to-date totals.

Payroll reports shall include payroll register, component summary, bank advice, department and cost-center costing, statutory summaries, tax summary, employer cost, and headcount-to-payroll reconciliation.

Accounting integration shall publish a PayrollRunFinalized event with totals by component, cost center, department, project and company; Finance posting rules (or the Accounting Export connector) create journals; employee-level detail remains in HRMIS and is reachable by drill-down.

The calculation engine shall be deterministic: the run freezes a snapshot of inputs (employee data, structures, attendance, tables, rules versions), so a recalculation with the same snapshot gives identical results. (new)
Each result shall carry a calculation trace (inputs, formulas, rule versions, rounding) viewable by authorized users. (new)
Results of a locked run shall be immutable; corrections are new entries in later runs referencing the original. (new)
Calculation shall run as a chunked, resumable job with progress, meeting GHR-01 (10,000 employees in under 15 minutes). (new)

A parallel-run tool shall import a legacy system's results, compare by employee and component against this system, classify differences, and produce a tolerance report used for go-live decisions. (new)
A what-if simulation shall estimate the payroll effect of a salary revision, policy or tax change before activation. (new, S)
Multi-entity and multi-currency payroll shall be supported, each entity with its own calendar, pay groups, bank accounts and posting dimensions. (new)
A payroll calendar with cut-off reminders and a readiness checklist (attendance locked, loans updated, claims approved, bank data complete) shall guide each run. (new)
Payroll records shall be retained and archived according to pack-defined legal periods, with restricted access and audit. (new)
Payslips and payroll information shall be available through the mobile application under the controls of MOB-80 to MOB-83 and MSEC-09, with the same permissions and masking as on the web.

Loan and advance types shall be configurable with eligibility (tenure, grade, existing loans), maximum amount (fixed or multiple of salary), interest (none, flat, reducing balance) and maximum tenure.
Applications shall route through approval workflows with finance review and optional guarantor.
Approved loans shall generate an installment schedule; recovery shall flow automatically into payroll.
Employees shall request early settlement, skip or restructuring; HR can hold or adjust installments with audit.
Outstanding loans shall appear in final settlement and offboarding clearance.
Perquisite tax on interest-free or concessional loans shall be configurable by country pack. (S)

Disbursement shall publish LoanDisbursed for Finance (employee receivable and payment) and installments recovered through payroll shall reduce it; the loan ledger shall reconcile to the Finance control account when licensed. (new)
Expense categories shall carry limits by grade, per-diem and mileage rules, receipt requirements and tax treatment.
Employees shall submit claims with receipts (camera capture on mobile, OCR to prefill amounts), multi-currency, project and cost center coding.
Policy checks at submission shall flag over limit, duplicate receipt, missing receipt and out-of-period items for approvers.
Travel requests shall support itinerary, advance and estimate, approval and settlement against actual expenses.
Approved claims shall be reimbursed through payroll or a separate payment batch.
Approved claims shall publish ExpenseClaimApproved so Finance posts the expense and employee payable, and payment status shall return to the claim. (new)
When Finance is licensed, budget availability shall be checked on submission or approval per the budget policy (document 5, BUD-06). (new, wave B)
Corporate card statements shall import and match to claims by reference, amount and date. (new, S)

Case management shall support grievances, complaints and incidents with confidential handling, restricted case teams and tamper-evident notes.
The disciplinary process shall be stage-configurable: allegation, show-cause notice, reply deadline, inquiry, hearing, decision and appeal, each with templates and legal timelines.
Harassment and sensitive cases shall use dedicated routing, committee assignment and anonymous reporting where enabled.
Union membership and collective agreement terms shall be recordable and applicable to relevant policies where the tenant uses them. (C)

Surveys (pulse, engagement, exit) shall support anonymity, segmentation, scheduling, reminders and result dashboards with minimum group size.
