HR shall issue assets to employees and record return with acknowledgement, using the Assets module register when licensed, or a lightweight HR register (type, serial number, status, condition) otherwise.
Unreturned assets shall appear in offboarding clearance and final settlement with recovery value.
Access cards, parking, lockers, desk booking and transport routes shall be manageable as bookable or assignable resources. (S)
Uniform and consumable issuance shall be tracked with entitlement cycles, using Inventory when licensed. (S)
Migrating the lightweight register to the Assets module shall be supported by an import template and link repair. (new)
Employees shall see the assets assigned to them and acknowledge receipt or request return on mobile and web
Headcount plans shall be created per unit with budget, growth assumptions and scenarios, linked to positions and requisitions (and to Finance budgets when licensed).
Succession plans shall identify critical roles, successors, readiness ratings and vacancy risk, with talent review sessions.
A skills inventory shall be maintained from profiles, learning and reviews, with internal mobility matching to open roles.
Employee records shall support national ID or residence permit (iqama) numbers with expiry, passport, work permit and visa data, sponsor or establishment, nationality, and GOSI number.
Social insurance contributions shall be computed from pack tables that differ by nationality, with contribution base rules, caps and monthly return files.
A wage protection file shall be generated in the required bank and platform format, with submission status, reconciliation and a compliance dashboard.
Saudization (national workforce classification) reporting shall compute ratios by entity and activity, with alerts and what-if hiring analysis.
End-of-service benefit calculation shall follow pack rules by termination type, contract type and tenure, feeding final settlement and Finance accrual.
Working-time and leave rules (weekend pattern, Ramadan hours, annual and sick leave tiers, Hajj, maternity and other statutory leave) shall be pack defaults with Hijri holiday calendars.
Contract types, probation limits, notice periods and termination reasons shall be configured by pack, with export or connector support for contract registration with national platforms.
Residence permit, visa, exit and re-entry and renewal tracking shall support workflows, reminders, fees and cost allocation per employee.
Medical insurance coverage for employees and dependents shall be tracked against regulatory minimums with expiry alerts.
Payslips, letters and certificates shall be bilingual (Arabic and English) with right-to-left layout and Hijri or Gregorian dates by company setting.
Payroll periods shall support Gregorian or Hijri month basis by company, and proration rules for each.
Hosting, personal-data handling and cross-border transfer settings shall follow the Saudi data protection requirements confirmed with local counsel, including regional hosting options.
Mobile attendance, location capture and task evidence for Saudi entities shall follow the data protection and labor requirements confirmed with local counsel
US legal entities shall capture EIN, state registrations, unemployment insurance accounts, workers compensation and payroll calendars.
US employee data shall include SSN (encrypted, masked, restricted view), work state and residence state, work authorization, federal W-4 and state withholding forms, and emergency contacts.
Worker classification shall distinguish W-2 employees and 1099 contractors, exempt and non-exempt status, and union status, with rules for each.
Employees working in multiple states shall be supported, with allocation of work days for tax and policy purposes.
Pronouns and voluntary self-identification fields (EEO categories, veteran and disability status) shall be separated from general HR views and available only for compliance reporting.
FLSA rules shall be configurable: overtime after 40 hours per week, daily overtime and double-time by state, meal and rest break rules, and premium pay.
PTO, vacation, sick and personal leave policies shall support accrual by hours worked, caps, carry-over and payout rules.
The US pack shall include state and local paid sick leave rules (accrual, usage, carry-over, reasons) and update through pack releases.
FMLA tracking shall determine eligibility, track entitlement, designate leave, generate required notices and support intermittent leave.
Jury duty, military leave and bereavement shall be supported with policy templates.
Timesheets shall support project, client and task coding, billable flag, approvals and lock for payroll (see FR-HRM-ATT-22).
The system shall send employee, compensation, time and deduction data to the payroll partner and receive calculated results, taxes, deductions and net pay for display and reporting.
Federal, state and local tax calculation, filing, deposit and year-end forms (941, W-2, W-3, 1099-NEC) shall be performed by the partner; the product shows status and documents.
Pre-tax and post-tax deductions, garnishments, child support orders and benefit deductions shall be maintained and synced.
Payment methods shall include direct deposit (ACH), paper check and pay card, with split deposits.
Off-cycle runs, bonuses, supplemental wages, tip reporting and reimbursements shall be supported through the partner.
A payroll reconciliation view shall compare partner output with product inputs and flag discrepancies.
The partner abstraction shall allow switching partners per tenant without changing HR data models. (S)
Partner payroll results shall publish PayrollRunFinalized in the same form as native payroll so Finance posting rules work unchanged. (new)
Plans (medical, dental, vision, life, disability, FSA, HSA, 401(k)) shall be configurable with eligibility, waiting periods, coverage tiers, rates and employer contributions.
Open enrollment shall run by period with decision support, dependents, beneficiary designation, confirmation statements and audit.
Qualifying life events shall open special enrollment windows with documents and deadlines.
Carrier file feeds shall transmit enrollments and changes in carrier formats; reconciliation reports highlight mismatches.
401(k) contributions shall flow to the plan administrator with deferral limits and match calculations.
COBRA qualifying events shall be detected, notices generated and tracked.
ACA measurement, offer tracking and 1094-C and 1095-C data preparation shall be supported.
Form I-9 shall be completed in Section 1 by the employee and Section 2 by an authorized representative with document capture, reverification dates and retention.
E-Verify submissions and results shall integrate through a connector. (S)
EEO-1 component data and reports shall be generated from self-identification and job category data.
New-hire reporting to state agencies shall be generated or transmitted through the partner.
OSHA injury and illness logs (300, 300A, 301) shall be maintained with reporting deadlines.
Required postings, policy acknowledgements and harassment training tracking by state shall be supported through learning compliance assignments.
Pay transparency, salary history and pay equity reports shall be configurable for states with such requirements.
US tenants shall be hosted in US regions with US-only support access options.
Controls shall align with SOC 2 Type II criteria; evidence collection and reports shall be supported.
State privacy requirements shall be supported through data access, correction and deletion workflows within legal retention rules.
Candidate and employee use of automated decision tools shall follow applicable bias-audit and notice requirements; such features are disabled by default where laws require review.
State and local requirements for notice and consent to electronic monitoring and location capture of employees shall be configurable by pack
Predictive models shall estimate attrition risk, absenteeism trends, time-to-fill and payroll cost projection, trained per tenant with transparency on features used. (wave D)
Every prediction shall show contributing factors and be restricted to authorized roles; individual-level predictions are off by default.
Pay equity analysis shall compare compensation across groups controlling for grade, tenure and location, with remediation planning.
Natural-language query over permitted data shall return charts and tables respecting the user's data scope (through the kernel semantic layer). (wave A to B)
An assistant shall answer employee questions on balances, policies, payslips and process steps using the employee's own data and the tenant's policy documents, with source references. (wave A)
HR users shall draft letters, job descriptions, policy summaries and review summaries with the assistant and edit before use. (wave A to B)
The assistant shall perform actions (apply for leave, raise a request) only after explicit user confirmation, through the same workflows and permissions as the UI.
Tenants shall disable AI per module, restrict data used, and review logs of AI interactions; payroll and compensation data can be excluded entirely.
AI shall not make or finalize hiring, disciplinary, termination or pay decisions; outputs in these areas are advisory with human review recorded.

AI features, including those available in the mobile application, shall not use location history or task evidence to infer behavior, rank employees or trigger actions, and location data shall be excluded from AI context unless a tenant explicitly enables a named use and the user holds the GPS evidence permission.
Extension points (custom tabs, widgets, actions, scripts, marketplace) are platform capabilities defined in the kernel and later waves; HRMIS exposes its objects and events to them. (wave D)
Attendance events, location evidence, task location events, status histories and decision histories are append-only; corrections are new records that reference the original.
Every event stores capture time and server receipt time separately, with the idempotency key and the policy version used for validation.
Location evidence and task location events are held apart from attendance results and task records, with stricter access and their own retention.
Evidence and event tables shall be partitioned by time with retention and purge jobs
Employees, organization units, locations, users, devices, documents and workflow records shall be referenced by id and never copied
Precise coordinates are classified sensitive; the encryption approach for coordinates versus aggregated analytics is decision MD-28; aggregated analytics shall use rounded or gridded locations.
Every new table shall pass the module table checklist of document 3, section 7.6.
All permissions of section 28.2 shall be registered in the Kernel permission registry and be assignable to roles through permission sets; baseline roles ship as editable defaults
The same permission and data scope shall govern web, mobile, API and AI access to the same data
Viewing GPS evidence and task locations shall be a distinct permission from viewing attendance or task status, off by default for senior management, and every use shall be logged.
Segregation of duties shall prevent a user from approving their own exceptions, regularizations, tasks or leave, and from reviewing a task they are assigned to
Delegated approval and out-of-office substitution shall carry only the delegator's permissions within the delegation period and be audited.
A System Administrator shall have no access to business data by default; infrastructure actions on devices are limited to the mobile platform's operational functions.
Purpose limitation: each category of location and activity data shall have a documented business purpose, and data shall not be used for other purposes.
Data minimization: only the configured events capture location; precision and retention are the minimum that serves the purpose; aggregated analytics are preferred to individual-level data.
Role-based access: location history and evidence are visible only to roles with the GPS evidence permission within their data scope; senior management access is off by default

Retention, archival and deletion: retention periods are configurable per data category, tenant and entity with country defaults from packs; expiry triggers audited purge or anonymization, honoring legal holds

Audit: every view, export and administrative change involving location evidence, task evidence, payroll data and personal documents is logged, and unusual patterns of evidence access raise alerts to the tenant's security contacts.

Employee transparency: before first capture, and when purposes or retention change, employees receive a plain-language notice in their language and acknowledge it; employees can see their own recorded events and locations
Secure storage and transmission: encrypted in transit and at rest; evidence files in the Kernel document store under tenant keys; secure document access as in MOB-70 to MOB-72.

A purpose register per tenant shall list each data category, purpose, legal or policy basis chosen by the customer, events, access roles and retention, and be exportable for audits and employee representatives.

A data protection impact assessment template shall be provided for enabling location capture, geo-fence modes and task location capture, and the features shall be enabled per entity only after the tenant confirms it.

Data residency shall follow the entity's hosting region; location evidence and media shall stay in that region
Supervisors and reviewers shall receive guidance and acknowledge acceptable use before receiving the GPS evidence permission; misuse is auditable.
Documentation for employee representatives or works councils, where customers need it, shall be generated from the purpose register.
No mobile feature shall be released before the backend services, Kernel extensions and policies it depends on are available and tested.
Each release shall include tests of the previous application version against the current API
Release M4 shall not add business functions that Android lacks, and any platform difference shall be documented
A release shall not ship with open severity-1 or severity-2 defects, open privacy findings on location features, or an unfinished retention job.

The module shall support at least 50,000 employees per tenant, with payroll for 10,000 employees completing in under 15 minutes and attendance processing for 500 employees on three shifts for a month in under 5 minutes

Data shall be classified as general personal, sensitive personal and restricted (cases, investigations); sensitive and restricted fields shall use field-level encryption, masking by default, restricted roles, and access logging
Every employee-related record that changes over time shall be effective-dated; as-of queries and timelines shall be available throughout
A backdated change shall show an impact analysis (attendance, leave, payroll, benefits) before saving and flag affected periods for recalculation (new)
Privacy tools shall support access, correction, export and erasure or anonymization within retention rules, legal holds, and statutory record-keeping periods defined by packs (new)
Salary and compensation data shall be hidden from every role except those explicitly granted, including in reports, exports, search results, AI and notifications
Multiple legal entities and countries shall be supported in one tenant with different calendars, policies and country packs
Statutory formats and rules shall change only through staged pack releases with impact preview
All HR actions on behalf of another person (HR applying leave for an employee, manager marking attendance) shall be audited with the acting user
Employee self-service and approvals shall work on mobile and low-bandwidth connections
Precise location, device identifiers and task evidence shall be collected only at configured business events, for documented purposes
Web and mobile clients shall use the same HRMIS APIs, business rules, workflows and Kernel authorization; no mobile-only authorization model or business rule shall exist
Every location-bearing record shall carry the event capture time, the server receipt time and the validation result, so offline and late submissions are distinguishable
Access to location history and evidence shall be restricted by role and data scope, logged, retention-limited and disclosed to employees through a notice and acknowledgement
Country-specific privacy, employment, working-time and statutory rules shall be configured through packs and validated by qualified local experts before release; none shall be hard-coded

The system shall keep a control-plane registry of tenants with name, status (provisioning, active, suspended, offboarding, deleted), region, cluster, environment type, and creation data.

The system shall provision a tenant from a template: create its database, run kernel and licensed-module migrations, install selected country and industry packs, seed roles, default workflows and numbering, create the first administrator, apply entitlements and run smoke tests.

Each tenant shall have its own database, file-store prefix, encryption keys, audit log and configuration. No query, job or API call shall cross tenant databases except explicit control-plane operations.
The tenant shall be resolved server-side from the host name, token or API key, and never from request payload fields.
The system shall support production, UAT and sandbox environments per tenant, with data masking rules applied when copying to non-production.
A tenant shall be assignable to a hosting region and clusters; moving a tenant between clusters or regions shall be supported by backup, restore and a connection switch with verification.
The on-premise package shall provision exactly one tenant with the same code, validating the license file instead of a subscription record.
Tenants shall have custom domain, branding (logo, colors, login page) and email sender identity.
The system shall suspend a tenant into read-only or locked state per the entitlement state machine without deleting data.
The system shall export a complete portable tenant package (data and configuration) and shall support scheduled deletion with a retention window and a deletion certificate. (S)
The system shall run fleet migrations across tenants in batches with canary tenants first, isolating a failed tenant in maintenance mode without stopping others.
A vendor user may access tenant business data only through a time-boxed, logged, tenant-approved support grant.

The system shall support multiple companies per tenant, each with country, base currency, optional group currency, tax IDs, fiscal calendar, holiday calendar, bank accounts, letterhead and default language.
The system shall support branches and locations under a company, with address, geo-coordinates and operating hours.
The system shall support configurable organization unit types (division, department, wing, directorate, team) with unlimited depth and effective dating.
The system shall support multiple hierarchy types on the same units (reporting, cost, geographic, project) (S).
The system shall support fiscal calendars of any start month, 4-4-5 or 13-period patterns, and adjustment periods, with period statuses (future, open, soft-closed, closed).
An organization unit shall optionally reference a Finance cost center; the reference shall remain empty when Finance is not licensed.
The system shall support inter-company relationships (parent, subsidiary, ownership percentage) for consolidation (wave B).
The tenant shall rename any standard label per language (for example Department to Wing).
The system shall support username and password with configurable policy (length, complexity, history, expiry, lockout), and password reset by verified email or SMS.
The system shall support multi-factor authentication (authenticator app, SMS or email code, hardware key) with enforcement per tenant, role or user.
The system shall support SSO through OIDC and SAML 2.0, and LDAP and Active Directory directory sync and authentication.
The system shall provide session management: configurable timeout, concurrent session limits, forced sign-out, device and session list for each user.
The system shall issue API keys and OAuth client credentials with scopes, expiry, IP allow lists and rate limits.
The system shall support user invitations, bulk user import, and automatic deprovisioning through SCIM (S).
Access shall be permission-based. Each module and kernel component registers permissions (resource, action) through its manifest; roles are sets of permissions; users hold multiple roles.
Permission sets shall be editable per tenant; baseline roles shipped by modules and packs are defaults only.
Data scopes shall restrict records by company, branch, department, hierarchy position (own, team, subtree) and attribute conditions, and be applied on every query, report and export.
Field-level security shall allow hidden, masked, read-only or editable per field and role, including custom fields.
Maker-checker shall be configurable on any sensitive action (permission change, posting rule change, payroll finalization, bank detail change, bulk export).
Segregation-of-duties rules shall be configurable (for example the creator of a payment cannot approve it) and checked at role assignment and at runtime; conflicts shall be reportable.
Temporary access and delegation shall be supported with start, end, reason and audit.
An access review report shall list users, roles, last login and sensitive permissions for periodic recertification. (S)
User and company limits from the entitlement shall be enforced when creating or activating users and companies.
Every setting shall declare key, type, default, validation, allowed layers (product, country pack, industry pack, tenant, company, role or user), visibility, and whether a change needs approval.
The system shall resolve effective values by layer with the most specific layer winning and shall show where each effective value came from.
Settings shall be searchable, grouped by module, with help text per language.
Changes shall be versioned, audited, exportable in configuration packages, and reversible to a prior version.
Feature flags shall switch capabilities on or off per tenant, company or user group, independent of entitlements (entitlements say what is allowed; flags say what is enabled).
Settings changes shall take effect without restart, with caching invalidated across hosts.

The system shall record, in the same transaction as the change, every create, update and delete with actor, timestamp, entity, record id, field-level before and after values, source (UI, API, import, job, AI) and correlation id.
The system shall record views and exports of fields classified sensitive, and authentication and security events (login, failure, MFA, permission change, key change, license change).
The audit log shall be append-only, tamper-evident through chained hashes, and not editable by any role including tenant admin.
Audit entries shall be searchable by user, entity, record, date and action, and exportable with permission.
Retention and archival of audit entries shall be configurable, with partitioned storage and verification of archived chains.
Changes made through AI shall be marked as AI-assisted, with the confirming user recorded.
A record's history view shall be available from every detail page to authorized users.
Numbering schemes shall be defined per document type, company, branch and fiscal year with prefix, suffix, date parts, padding, reset rule (never, yearly, monthly) and starting value.
A scheme shall be gap-allowed or gap-free; gap-free schemes allocate at posting time under lock and never skip on rollback.
Numbers shall be assigned by the system on save or post according to the document type, and never editable afterwards.
Manual numbering with uniqueness check shall be selectable where law or practice requires. (S)
Voided numbers shall be retained with status and reason, and a void report shall exist for gap-free series.
Numbering shall support concurrent users without duplicates under load.
A business partner shall have one or more roles (supplier, customer, both, bank, tax authority, carrier, other) and role-specific data, so the same record serves purchasing and selling.
A partner shall hold multiple addresses (billing, shipping, registered), contacts, bank accounts, tax registrations (per country), payment terms, currency, credit limit, and classification tags.
Partners may be scoped to all companies in the tenant or to specific companies.
The system shall detect probable duplicates on create (tax ID, name similarity, bank account) and offer merge with full audit and re-pointing of references through registered contracts.
Bank account changes shall use maker-checker by default and notify designated approvers.
Partner status (draft, active, on hold, blocked, archived) shall control whether new transactions are allowed, with reason codes.
Partner onboarding shall be configurable as a workflow with required documents, approvals and expiry reminders (for example tax certificates). (S)
Custom fields, layouts and validation shall apply to partners through the metadata engine.
Tax ID formats shall be validated per country through packs (for example NTN and CNIC in Pakistan, VAT number in KSA, EIN in the United States).

The catalog shall hold items of configurable types (stock item, non-stock item, service, expense category, fixed-asset class, bundle) with code, multilingual name, description, category, status and images.
Categories shall form a configurable hierarchy with inherited defaults (tax code, accounts, units).
Units of measure and conversion tables shall support multiple units per item (base, purchase, sales, stock), with rounding rules, and global and item-specific conversions.
Item attributes and variants (size, color, grade) shall be configurable per category, with variant generation. (S)
Items shall support multiple identifiers (SKU, barcode, supplier part number, manufacturer part number) with uniqueness rules.

Module-specific attributes (valuation method, batch and serial tracking, depreciation class, reorder rules) shall be added to items by the owning module without altering the kernel table, and shall appear only when that module is licensed.
Items may be scoped to all companies or to specific companies.
Price lists and effective-dated prices shall be supported by Procurement and Sales using catalog references; the catalog itself holds only standard cost and standard price defaults.
Bulk import, export and mass update shall be supported with validation and preview.
The system shall hold tax codes, rates, effective dates, jurisdictions, tax accounts (by reference), and applicability (sales, purchase, both).
Tax determination shall combine item or category, partner, company, jurisdiction, document type and date through configurable rules.
The engine shall support inclusive and exclusive pricing, compound taxes, multiple taxes per line, withholding taxes at document or payment level, exemptions with certificates, and rounding policy.
Tax rules shall be effective-dated so past documents recompute correctly and rate changes apply by document date.
Country packs shall provide codes, rules, returns and statutory report layouts; tenants may extend them without overwriting the pack.
An integration point shall let a connector call an external tax service (for example a US sales-tax rate service) for determination.
Tax calculation shall return a trace explaining each tax line for audit and support.
The system shall support English, Urdu and Arabic at launch with right-to-left mirroring of layouts, and further languages through translation catalogs and language packs.
Users shall choose language, time zone, date format, calendar (Gregorian or Hijri display), number format and first day of week; companies set defaults.

Dates shall be stored in Gregorian and rendered in the user's calendar; Hijri conversion shall be configurable by method (for example Umm al-Qura) and support manual moon-sighting adjustments for religious-holiday calendars.

Currencies shall be configurable with codes, symbols, decimals and rounding; exchange rates shall support multiple rate types (daily, average, budget), manual entry, import, and a connector for automatic feeds.
Translation of master data names and labels shall be managed through the admin UI with export and import for translators, and missing translations shall fall back to a configured language.
Holiday calendars shall be defined per company, branch or location, with packs providing national holidays.
All generated documents and notifications shall render in the recipient's language where a template exists.
Search shall normalize Arabic and Urdu text (diacritics, letter variants, digit systems).

Admins shall add custom fields to any extensible entity (types: text, long text, number, decimal, money, date, date-time, boolean, single and multi-select, lookup to another entity, user, file, formula) with label per language, help text, default, validation, uniqueness, and conditional visibility or requirement.
Custom fields shall be permission-controlled per role (hidden, read-only, editable) and carried through APIs, imports, exports, reports and workflows.
Option lists shall be reusable, effective-dated and translatable.
Frequently filtered fields shall be promotable to indexed storage by an admin action with impact warning. (S)
Deleting a custom field shall be a soft retire that hides the field and keeps its data until an explicit purge.

Admins shall define custom objects (entity name, fields, relationships to existing entities, list and form layouts, numbering, status model, permissions, workflow hooks) and manage records through generated screens and APIs. (wave B for full relationships; basic objects in wave A)
Custom objects shall be reportable through the semantic layer and available in workflows and rules.
Form layouts shall be configurable per entity, role and company: sections, tabs, field order, columns, read-only rules, conditional sections, and mobile variants.
List layouts shall support column sets, default filters, grouping, totals, row actions and saved views shared by user, role or company.
Labels and terminology shall be overridable per language and layer.
Navigation menus shall be configurable per role, with ordering, grouping, icons, links to reports and external URLs.

Each document type shall have a status model (states, allowed transitions, who may transition, required fields per state, automatic actions) defined as data; modules ship defaults and tenants may adjust within module-defined safe limits.
Statuses that carry accounting or legal meaning (posted, finalized, closed) shall be locked against removal.
Workflow definitions shall be created per document type with steps, conditions, approver resolution and outcomes, stored as versioned data and edited in a visual designer.
Approver resolution shall support named user, role, organization hierarchy (manager, manager's manager, department head), position, partner or document field, expression, and queue with claim.
Conditions shall use the rules engine (for example amount thresholds, department, item category, risk flags) to choose routes and skip steps.
Steps shall support sequential, parallel (all or any, quorum), and conditional branching. (parallel and conditional in wave B)
Delegation and out-of-office substitution shall be configurable by date range, with audit of who acted for whom.
SLAs shall define reminders and escalations by elapsed time, working calendar and priority. (S in wave A, M in wave B)
Approvers shall be able to approve, reject with reason, request changes, reassign, or ask for information, with comments and attachments; all decisions shall be kept in a decision history.
The approval inbox shall list pending tasks across modules with filters, bulk approval where allowed, mobile access and email or push deep links.
The engine shall prevent self-approval and apply segregation-of-duties rules from IAM.
Running instances shall stay on the version they started with; new versions apply to new instances unless migrated explicitly.
Workflows shall support automated steps (send notification, call webhook, set field, create document, run job) with retry and failure handling.
A simulator shall run a definition against sample documents and show the route before activation.
Long-running orchestration (multi-day, event-driven) may use a separate engine behind the same task model; approvals stay in the native engine. (C)

The engine shall evaluate expressions in a sandbox with typed variables supplied by each rule context, an allowed function library (math, date, string, lookup, aggregation over provided collections), and no access to files, network or reflection.
Each evaluation shall have time and memory limits and fail safely with a clear error.
Rule types shall include validation (block or warn), default value, calculation, eligibility, routing condition, determination (for example account, tax code, price), and notification condition.

Rules shall be authored through a guided editor with autocomplete of available variables and functions, syntax check, and plain-language rendering, and through a table-style decision table for common cases.
Every rule shall be versioned, effective-dated, testable against sample data and saved test cases, and reversible to a prior version.
Activation of rules in sensitive contexts (posting, payroll, tax) shall require maker-checker and a passing test suite.
Rule evaluation shall produce a trace (inputs, branches taken, output) available to support and auditors.
A dependency view shall show which workflows, templates and policies use a rule before it is changed.
Heavy repeated evaluation (payroll for thousands of employees) shall run through compiled or cached expressions meeting the performance targets of the consuming module.
Channels shall include in-app, email, SMS, WhatsApp Business (through a gateway), and mobile push, each with a pluggable provider and delivery log.
Templates shall be configurable per event, channel and language, with placeholders from the event context, preview, and test send.
Subscriptions and triggers shall be rule-based (for example notify the line manager when leave is requested, notify finance when a payment run fails) and configurable per tenant and company.
Users shall set channel preferences and quiet hours, except for notifications marked mandatory.
Notifications shall be queued, retried with back-off, deduplicated, rate limited, and visible in a delivery log with status and failure reasons.
Digest and batching shall be supported for noisy events. (S)
Email sending shall support tenant-specific sender identity, SPF and DKIM guidance, and bounce handling.
Any record may carry attachments with type, description, version, expiry date and permissions inherited from the record.
Storage shall be abstracted (local disk, network share, S3-compatible) with checksum, size and type validation, a configurable virus-scan hook, and per-tenant encryption.
Versioning shall keep prior versions with who and when, and allow restore.
Retention rules shall define how long document types are kept and what happens afterwards (archive, delete, legal hold).

A template engine shall generate letters, vouchers, invoices, payslips, labels and statutory forms from data and templates with conditional blocks, tables, images, barcodes and QR codes, in PDF, Word and HTML.
A visual template designer shall edit headers, footers, letterheads, fonts and layouts per company and language, with versioning and preview against sample records.
Generated documents may be stored against the record, signed (digital signature, e-signature connector), emailed, and watermarked by status (draft, approved).
Expiry tracking shall raise reminders for documents that expire (licenses, contracts, certificates).
Every module capability shall be exposed through a versioned REST API with OpenAPI, consistent filtering, sorting, cursor pagination, idempotency keys, and bulk endpoints.
Webhooks shall deliver configured events with signed payloads, retries with back-off, a dead-letter queue, replay, and a delivery log.

Import and export templates shall be configurable: file formats (CSV, Excel, JSON, XML), column mapping, transformations, validation preview, error report, and rollback of an import batch where feasible.
A bulk data loader shall process large files asynchronously with progress, restartability and duplicate handling; target 50,000 rows per file.

A connector framework shall define a standard adapter contract for banks, tax portals, e-invoicing services, biometric devices, SMS and email gateways, and accounting export, with configuration, credentials in secret storage, health checks and logs.
A scheduled file-exchange facility (SFTP, shared folder) shall support inbound and outbound jobs with archiving.
API clients shall be rate limited, throttled per tenant, and observable (usage, errors, latency) with alerts.
Sandbox endpoints and test data shall be available to partners per tenant environment.
Accounting Export connector: when Finance is not licensed, subledger events shall be exportable as journals to files or to external accounting systems with configurable account mapping.
Jobs shall be defined with schedule (cron-like, calendar-aware), parameters, owner, retry policy, concurrency limit, timeout and priority.
Long-running jobs shall run in chunks with checkpoints so they resume after restart, and expose progress, logs, and cancel.
The job center shall show running, queued, failed and completed jobs for the tenant with filters, rerun, and download of results.
Per-tenant concurrency caps and fair scheduling shall stop one tenant's jobs from starving others.
Jobs shall be cluster-safe: a job runs once even with multiple workers.
Operational alerts shall fire for failed, stuck or overdue jobs, outbox lag, and failed postings.

An entitlement shall define deployment type, edition, licensed modules and feature keys, packs and add-ons, limits (named users, concurrent users, companies, active employees, storage, API calls, AI tokens), term, maintenance expiry, support tier, source flag, and optional server binding.
On-premise entitlements shall come from a signed license file verified offline against an embedded public key; SaaS entitlements from the control-plane subscription.
The module loader shall load only licensed modules; unlicensed modules' schemas, menus, APIs and screens shall not exist for the tenant.
The state machine (active, warning, grace, read-only, locked) shall drive behavior with banners, admin emails and a license page, and shall allow exporting data in read-only and locked states.
Limits shall be enforced at the point of use with soft warnings (default 90 percent) and hard stops, with clear messages and an administrator view of consumption.
Usage metering shall record active users, active employees, companies, storage, API calls and AI tokens monthly and produce a usage statement per tenant.
Checks shall occur at startup, module load, periodically and at multiple independent points; clock rollback shall be detected from several stores.
License renewal, upgrade (more modules or users), and re-issue after hardware change shall be possible by uploading a new signed file, without reinstalling.
A maintenance expiry shall block installing releases newer than the maintenance date while leaving the installed version usable (perpetual licenses).
The vendor-side issuer tool shall produce licenses with unique ids, support revocation lists for online-connected installs, and keep its private key offline.
Optional online activation and usage reporting shall be off by default and enabled only with the customer's consent.

summary: Packs (country, industry, template, connector, language) shall be signed, versioned bundles with a manifest of contents, compatible product versions, dependencies and merge rules.

basis: Pack install needed for Pakistan pack
summary: Installing or upgrading a pack shall preserve tenant overrides, report conflicts for review, and never alter posted transactional data.

basis: Pack install needed for Pakistan pack
summary: The system shall show pack contents, versions, available updates, and release notes; upgrades shall be previewed with a change report and applied through maker-checker.
All configuration objects shall be exportable as a configuration package with checksum, diffable against another environment, and importable with validation.
Promotion from sandbox or UAT to production shall run validation, dependency checks and automated tests where defined, take a rollback snapshot, and require approval.
Configuration history shall show who changed what and when, with the ability to roll back a package.

basis: Pack install needed for Pakistan pack
summary: Pack authoring tools (vendor side) shall validate manifests and test packs against a clean tenant before release.
AI requests shall pass through a gateway that selects provider and model by tenant policy and region (hosted, regional or local), and hides provider details from skills.
Skills shall be registered by modules with name, description, input schema, tools they may call (module contracts), permission requirements, and evaluation tests.
The AI shall act only with the permissions of the requesting user; tool calls shall go through the same authorization, data scope and field security as the UI.
Any action that changes data shall be proposed first and executed only after explicit user confirmation through the same commands, validations and workflows as the UI.

The AI shall not post journals, approve transactions, finalize payroll, or make hiring, disciplinary, termination or compensation decisions; outputs in these areas are advisory with human review recorded.
Retrieval over tenant documents (policies, contracts, help) shall use a tenant-scoped index that honors document permissions and cites sources.
Tenants shall switch AI on or off per module and per user group, restrict data classes sent to external providers, choose provider and region, and review all AI interaction logs.
Usage shall be metered by tokens and calls per tenant and module, with limits and alerts that tie to entitlements.
Prompts shall be versioned in a registry; skills shall have evaluation sets run before each release; safety tests for prompt injection and data leakage shall run in CI.
Content from documents and external sources shall be treated as untrusted input and shall not be able to trigger tool calls on its own.

Configuration assistant: given a plain-language request, the AI shall produce a draft configuration package (fields, layouts, workflow, rules, report) for review, diff and sandbox test, and never apply it to production directly.
Natural-language query: questions shall be translated into semantic-layer queries, shown to the user in readable form, and executed within the user's scope.
Each portal type (supplier, customer, carrier, partner) shall have its own authentication realm; external identities shall never share accounts, sessions or credentials with internal users.

External users shall be created by invitation or by approved self-registration, with email verification, multi-factor authentication, optional single sign-on, and account recovery that never reveals whether an account exists.
Every external account shall link to a business partner and see only that partner's data, through portal-specific permissions and data scopes defined by the owning module.
Portals shall support tenant branding, custom domains, languages (English, Urdu, Arabic with right-to-left layout), and a reduced navigation set.
Partner administrators shall manage their own users within limits set by the tenant, with audit.
Portal traffic shall be rate limited and protected against automated abuse; uploads shall be scanned and size limited; all actions shall be audited and anomalies alerted.
A message center shall let internal and external users exchange messages and attachments on a record, using the collaboration component with an external visibility scope.
Portal APIs shall be separate from internal APIs, versioned, and unable to reach internal endpoints or other partners' data; isolation tests shall run in every pipeline.
The number of external users shall be metered against the entitlement (portal.external\_users); blocking a partner shall disable its external accounts automatically.
Access reviews and inactivity expiry shall be available for external accounts.
A device registry shall record each registered device (user, platform, app version, status, last sync), with per-user device limits, remote lock and remote wipe.

The sync protocol shall pull changes by scope (what a user or role may hold offline, for example a warehouse or a route), push queued actions, use delta tokens, be resumable and compressed, and be versioned.
Each device shall keep an outbox of pending actions with idempotency keys, retry and visible status; the server shall record received actions so repeats never duplicate documents.

Modules shall declare, in their manifests, conflict rules per entity type (server wins, merge fields, last write wins for low-risk fields, manual resolution); conflicts shall be recorded and presented to users with clear choices.

Local storage shall be encrypted with keys bound to the user session; data shall be wiped on logout, deprovisioning, wipe command or after a maximum offline period; field security shall be applied before data is synced, and masked fields shall not be synced unless allowed.
Modules shall declare which commands may be completed offline and which require server confirmation (financial postings and approvals are confirmed by the server before being shown as done).
Attachments (photos, signatures, scans) shall sync in chunks with resume.
Sync health (failures, backlog, conflicts, devices not seen) shall be monitored per tenant and device and shown to administrators.
A minimum app version shall be enforceable, and the API shall remain compatible with the previous app version so field staff are not blocked mid-shift.
Device clock differences shall be detected and recorded; server time shall be authoritative for audit; location tampering checks shall be available. (S)
Selective sync limits (item counts, data age, size) shall be configurable per module, with refresh policies for large reference data such as catalogs and price lists.
Modules shall declare searchable entities (documents, partners, items, employees, assets) with searchable fields and display templates; indexing shall follow change events within seconds.
Results shall be filtered by the requesting user's permissions, data scopes and field security at query time, and shall never reveal the existence of records the user cannot see.

Search shall normalize English, Urdu and Arabic text (diacritics, letter variants, digit systems), tolerate typing errors, support prefix and code lookups, and optionally transliterate between scripts. (transliteration, S)
A command palette shall combine search results with screens, reports, settings and actions, showing recents and favorites.
Ranking shall consider exact code matches, recency and usage, with facets by entity type and company.

Results shall return in under 300 milliseconds at the 95th percentile on 10 million indexed records per tenant; the default index shall use the tenant database's text search facilities and be replaceable behind the same interface.
Sensitive fields shall be excluded from the index by classification; administrators shall see index status, rebuild it, and manage exclusions.
AI retrieval over documents (document 9, section 14) shall use its own permission-aware index and shall not share storage with this search index.

Any record or document type that enables it shall support comment threads with mentions, attachments, edit and delete rules, and audit; visibility shall be internal or, for portals, shared with the external partner.
Tasks and reminders shall be creatable on records, assignable to users or groups, with due dates, recurrence and status, appearing on the user's home page and integrating with workflow tasks.
A per-record activity feed shall combine changes, comments, workflow events and documents, with filters.
Users shall follow records and choose notification preferences for comments, mentions, assignments and status changes.
Mentions and assignments shall notify through the notification component; reply by email shall add a comment where the tenant enables it. (S)
Comment visibility shall inherit record permissions; sensitive record types may disable comments; retention and legal hold shall apply.
Compliance export and deletion of comments shall be available to authorized roles with audit.

A print service shall manage printers by location and type (network document printers, label printers using standard label languages, cheque printers), with print agents for on-premise and desktop environments, queues, retries and routing by document type and location.
Label and barcode printing shall use templates with barcodes and QR codes (including GS1 formats), support batch printing and reprint control with audit.
Print jobs shall be logged with status and errors, restricted by permission, and available for reprint within retention rules.
The analytics API (REST and OData) of document 9 (ADH-10) shall be part of the public API, subject to the same authentication, scope, field security and rate limits, and metered with other API usage.
Every tenant-scoped table shall carry `tenant_id`, set by the platform and never accepted from a client.
A tenant shall be placed in dedicated mode (own database) or pooled mode (shared database with row-level security). Placement is a control-plane property; application code shall not branch on it.
In pooled mode the database session shall be bound to one tenant for the life of a request, and the application role shall be unable to bypass the isolation policies.
A tenant shall be movable from pooled to dedicated mode by export and import with verification, without schema change.
The isolation test suite shall run in both modes on every build. Pooled mode shall not be offered commercially before an independent security review passes.

Where Finance is not licensed, the kernel shall satisfy the Finance posting contract with a stub that records an accounting event for later export (the Accounting Export connector). Modules shall not test whether Finance is present (Doc 16, FR-XM-02).
