A global search (keyboard shortcut) shall find settings, users, roles, fields, workflows, templates, jobs and help, and open them directly.
Every list in the console shall support filters, sorting, column selection, saved views, bulk actions where meaningful, and export.
Every configuration object shall show status (draft, active, retired), version, last changed by and when, and a history tab.
Changes shall be saved as drafts, previewed, validated, and then published; publishing in production may require maker-checker according to settings.
The console shall show an environment banner (production, UAT, sandbox) on every page and prevent accidental production edits through a confirmation step when configured.
A dependency panel shall show what uses an object (for example which workflows use a role) before it is changed or retired.
A change summary and diff shall be shown before publishing and stored with the change.
Contextual help shall be available on every screen, with links to documentation and the AI assistant where enabled.

A first-run wizard shall guide the tenant admin through: company profile, country and industry pack selection, language and calendar, currency and fiscal year, modules to enable (within the entitlement), organization structure, first users and roles, and notification and email settings.
The wizard shall create everything through the same engines as manual setup and shall be resumable, skippable by step, and repeatable for additional companies.

A readiness checklist per module shall show required configuration (for example chart of accounts loaded, periods open, numbering set, approvers defined) with status and links, and shall block go-live of a module until mandatory items are complete unless overridden with a reason.
The wizard shall offer to import master data from templates (chart of accounts, partners, items, employees) through the import center with validation previews.
Implementation partners shall be able to work in a tenant with delegated, time-limited permissions and a visible project mode that records configuration work. (S)
The AI configuration assistant, where enabled, shall be offered in the wizard to draft fields, workflows and reports from plain-language descriptions, always as drafts for review. (S)
The user list shall show name, username, email, status, roles, companies, last login, MFA state and license seat consumption, with filters on any of these.

Admins shall create users individually, invite by email with expiring links, or import in bulk from a template with validation and a preview of errors; imports shall create invitations rather than passwords.
User statuses shall be invited, active, locked, disabled, and archived, with allowed transitions, reasons, and effects on sessions and workflow tasks (reassignment prompt on disable).
Each user record shall show profile, roles with effective dates and scope, data scopes, delegations, devices and sessions, MFA devices, login history, and recent activity from the audit log.
Admins shall reset passwords by sending a link, force password change, unlock accounts, revoke sessions, and enroll or reset MFA, each with an audit entry.
User groups and teams shall be definable for assignment of roles, notifications and data scopes in bulk.
Users may link to an employee record when HRMIS is licensed; the link is optional and managed from either side.
Licensed seat consumption (named, concurrent) shall be visible with warnings at configurable thresholds, and creation shall stop at the hard limit with an explanatory message.
Bulk actions shall include assign or remove role, change company, disable, extend access end date, and export.
Self-service profile pages shall let users manage their own language, time zone, calendar, notification preferences, MFA devices, active sessions and personal API tokens if permitted.

A permission preview mode ('view as role' or 'test as user') shall let administrators see menus and screens as a given role would, in a read-only simulation that cannot post or change data and is audited. (S)

Offboarding checklist: disabling a user shall show open tasks, owned documents and scheduled jobs for reassignment, and optionally trigger deprovisioning of linked directory accounts through SCIM or LDAP.
Admins shall configure password policy (length, complexity, history, expiry, lockout thresholds) per tenant, with optional stricter policy for privileged roles.
MFA policy shall be configurable per tenant, role, or user, with allowed methods and grace periods for enrollment.

SSO configuration screens shall support OIDC and SAML identity providers with metadata import, claim and role mapping, test sign-in, just-in-time provisioning rules, and the option to keep local admin break-glass accounts.
Directory configuration shall support LDAP and Active Directory connections with attribute mapping, group-to-role mapping, scheduled sync, and a test and dry-run view.
Session policy shall configure idle timeout, absolute timeout, concurrent session limit and remember-device duration.
Network policy shall allow IP allow lists per tenant, role or API client, and optional country restrictions. (S)
The permission catalog shall be browsable by module and resource with descriptions, sensitivity flags and the roles that hold each permission.

The role designer shall create roles by selecting permissions with search and module grouping, copy from baseline or another role, compare two roles side by side, and show the number of users holding the role.
Baseline roles shipped by modules and packs shall be copied into the tenant and editable; a pack upgrade shall propose, not force, changes to baseline roles.
Role assignment shall support company scope, start and end dates, reason, and approval through maker-checker for sensitive roles.
An effective-access viewer shall answer 'can this user do X on this record, and why' by showing the roles, scopes and rules that grant or deny the action.

The data scope designer shall define scopes by company, branch, department, hierarchy position (own, team, subtree), and attribute conditions, with a test that lists the records a sample user would see.
The field security matrix shall set hidden, masked, read-only or editable per field, per role, for standard and custom fields, with a preview of a form under a role.
Segregation-of-duties rules shall be definable from pairs of permissions or role combinations, with severity; the console shall report existing conflicts and block or warn on new assignments.
Delegations and temporary access shall be created by admins or by users within allowed limits, with automatic expiry and audit.
Access reviews shall let admins launch periodic recertification campaigns: managers or owners confirm or revoke each user's roles within a due date, with reminders and a report. (S)
A permission change report shall list who changed which role or assignment when, and a role usage report shall list unused permissions and inactive users.
Export and import of roles as part of configuration packages shall be supported.
A security dashboard shall show failed logins, locked accounts, MFA coverage, privileged users, API keys near expiry, stale accounts, license state and recent security events.
API client management shall create clients and keys with scopes, expiry, IP allow lists and rate limits; show the secret once; rotate, revoke, and show last use and usage statistics.
Alert rules shall notify designated users on configurable security events (for example repeated failures, new admin, bulk export, permission change, license change).
An encryption and keys page shall show key status (version, rotation date, next rotation) and allow initiating rotation where the deployment mode permits, with progress and audit.
Data classification shall let admins mark fields as sensitive, which drives masking, audit of views and export approval.

Privacy tools shall handle data subject requests: locate personal data across modules for a person, export it, and execute erasure or anonymization subject to retention rules and legal holds, with a case record and audit.
Export controls shall configure which exports need approval, row limits, and watermarking.
A login page and notification branding page shall set tenant branding, terms notices, and a login banner.

Support access grants raised by the vendor shall appear for tenant admin approval with scope, reason and duration, can be revoked at any time, and every action taken under a grant is shown in the audit viewer.

Company setup shall capture legal name, multilingual names, country, base and group currency, registrations (tax IDs and others with validity dates), bank accounts, default language, calendars and letterhead, with country-pack validation of formats.
Branch and location screens shall support address, map pin, time zone, and operating hours.
The organization chart editor shall show units as a tree and a diagram, support drag and drop re-parenting with effective dates, bulk import, and compare versions as of two dates.
Unit types, labels and hierarchy kinds shall be maintainable by the tenant, including renaming standard terms per language.

The fiscal calendar manager shall create years and periods from patterns, adjust period dates before use, open and close periods by module with checks and a closing checklist, and show who closed what.
A company switcher shall be available to users with multiple companies, with the active company clearly shown on every screen.
Company-level settings overrides shall be visible from the company page with a link to the settings center.
Each designer shall autosave drafts, validate continuously with plain-language errors, show a live preview with sample data, and list impacted objects before publishing.
Each object shall be versioned with comparison between versions and one-click revert to a prior version.
Each designer shall support export and import of its objects as configuration packages and as JSON for support purposes.
Designers shall be permission-controlled separately (for example a role can edit forms but not workflows).
All text in a designer (labels, help, messages) shall be translatable per language with a side-by-side translation view.

The field designer shall list fields by entity, with type, usage, status and promoted-index flag; creation shall use a guided form for types, validation (min, max, pattern, list), default, uniqueness, conditional visibility and requirement, and role permissions.
Option lists shall be managed centrally with effective dates, translations, ordering and import.

The object designer shall create custom objects with fields, relationships, numbering, status model, permissions, forms and lists in one guided flow, with generated screens and API documentation available immediately.
Retiring a field or object shall show the data volume and dependencies and soft-retire with an explicit later purge. (M)
The field designer shall warn about performance impact when enabling filters or sorts on custom fields in large tables and offer promotion to indexed storage. (S)

The form designer shall provide drag and drop layout of sections, tabs, columns and fields, conditional sections and fields (by value, role, status), read-only and required rules, field help, and separate mobile variants.
The form designer shall configure line-item grids (columns, order, defaults, inline calculations, totals) for document entities.
The list designer shall configure default columns, filters, grouping, sorting, totals, row colors by condition, row actions, bulk actions, and quick filters.
Layouts shall be assignable per role, company or branch, with a visible precedence order and a test-as-role preview.
The menu designer shall arrange navigation per role with groups, ordering, icons, links to reports, dashboards and external URLs, and hide entries by entitlement and permission automatically.
Labels and terminology shall be editable in a searchable table with per-language values and a view of where each label appears.

The status model designer shall display states and transitions as a diagram, set who may transition, required fields per state and automatic actions, and shall block removal of states with locked meanings.

The numbering designer shall build patterns from tokens (prefix, company code, branch code, year, month, sequence), show example numbers, set reset rule and gap-free option, and show the next number and void history.
Changes to numbering after use shall create a new version applying from a chosen date and never renumber existing documents.

The workflow designer shall provide a visual canvas for steps, conditions, parallel branches, approver resolution, escalation and automated actions, with a palette of step types and templates from packs.
Approver resolution shall be configured through pickers (user, role, hierarchy level, document field, expression) with a preview of who would be resolved for a sample document.
A simulator shall run the workflow against sample or recent documents, show the route taken and resolved approvers, and flag steps that cannot resolve an approver.
An instance monitor shall show running instances by definition, with stuck or overdue items, the ability to reassign, and migration of running instances to a new version when allowed.
Delegation rules and out-of-office settings shall be administrable centrally and by users for themselves.
Workflow analytics shall show cycle times, bottleneck steps, rejection rates and SLA breaches.
The rules editor shall offer a guided condition builder, a decision-table editor, and an expression editor with autocomplete, function help, syntax checking and a plain-language rendering.
Each rule shall have saved test cases with expected results, a run-all-tests action, and a trace view showing which branch produced the result.
The editor shall show where each rule is used and block deactivation of rules in use unless a replacement is chosen.
Rules in sensitive contexts (posting, payroll, tax) shall require passing tests and maker-checker to activate.

The template designer shall edit print and letter templates visually with fields, tables, conditionals, images, barcodes and QR codes, header and footer, page setup, language variants, and preview against real sample records.
Template assignments shall be by document type, company, branch and language, with default fallbacks.
The notification designer shall configure events, audiences, conditions, channels, templates per language, throttling and mandatory flags, with test send.
A delivery log shall show messages with status, retries and failure reasons, and allow resend.
The settings center shall list all settings by module and area with search, showing name, description, current effective value, source layer, default, last change and who changed it.
Setting editors shall be typed (toggle, number, choice, list, account or entity picker, expression) with validation, units, and help text in the user's language.
A layered view shall show the value at product, pack, tenant, company and role levels with override and reset-to-inherited actions.
Settings requiring approval shall create a change request with maker-checker; others apply immediately with audit.
Compare shall show setting differences between two companies or two environments, with the ability to copy values.
Settings history shall be browsable and any change reversible.
Feature flags shall be listed with description, scope and state, with owner and expected removal date for temporary flags. (S)
A recommended-settings advisor shall flag risky or inconsistent combinations (for example gap-free numbering with manual numbering, base currency changes after posting) and suggest fixes. (S)
Import and export of settings shall be supported through configuration packages.
Language management shall enable languages, set the default and fallback, and show translation completeness per module.

A translation workbench shall list strings with source and target side by side, status (missing, machine-suggested, reviewed), export and import in standard formats, and optional AI-assisted suggestions that require review.
Currency management shall maintain currencies and rate types, rate tables with manual entry and import, rate source connectors, and a rate gap report.
Calendar management shall maintain holiday calendars by company, branch and location, import holidays from packs, and manage Hijri adjustments by method and manual overrides.
Format settings shall set date, time, number, address and name formats per company and user default.
The administrator shall be able to preview any screen or document in a chosen language and direction.
The API console shall list clients and keys (SEC), show interactive API documentation by module and version, and a sandbox for trying calls.
The webhook manager shall register endpoints, choose events, show signing secrets once, test deliver, and display delivery logs with retry, replay and dead-letter handling.

The connector manager shall list available connectors (banks, tax portals, e-invoicing, biometric devices, messaging, accounting export), with configuration forms, credential storage, health checks, last run, and logs.
The import template designer shall map source columns to fields with transformations, lookups, defaults and validations, test with a sample file and save templates for reuse and schedule.
The file exchange manager shall configure scheduled inbound and outbound SFTP or folder jobs with archiving and error handling.
An integration monitor shall show volumes, error rates, latency and recent failures per client, connector and webhook with alerts.
The Accounting Export connector shall let admins map events and accounts to an external accounting format when Finance is not licensed.

The import center shall run imports of master and transactional data through templates, show validation results before commit, process asynchronously with progress, produce error files, and support rollback of a batch where feasible.
Bulk update shall let permitted admins change fields on filtered record sets with preview, approval for large changes, and audit.
The duplicate manager shall find and merge duplicate partners, items and employees using configurable match rules, with a review queue and merge audit.
The export center shall run permitted exports with approval rules, row limits, watermarking, and a log; exports of sensitive data require reason capture.
An AI-assisted migration assistant shall propose column mappings and flag data issues for human review before import. (S)
Archival management shall show data volumes by module, apply retention rules, and run archive jobs with verification.
Environment management shall create sandbox or UAT copies with masking profiles, refresh them on request, and compare configuration between environments before promotion.
Backup status shall show last successful backups, restore points and verification results; on-premise installs shall offer start, schedule and restore-to-sandbox actions subject to permission.
A portable tenant export shall package data and configuration for exit or migration, with integrity checks.
The job center shall list scheduled, queued, running, failed and completed jobs with filters, progress, logs, results, rerun, cancel, and schedule editing for permitted jobs.

The audit viewer shall search the change log, access log and security events by user, record, entity, date, action and source (UI, API, import, job, AI), show field-level differences, export with approval, and verify chain integrity on demand.
The record history view (from any record) shall show the same data scoped to that record for users with permission.
The notification log shall show sent, failed and queued messages with resend.

A system health page shall show service status, queue depth, outbox lag, failed postings, storage use, database size, slow queries summary, background worker status and the last backup, with alert subscriptions.
The posting exception queue (provided by the owning modules) shall be reachable from operations, showing failed cross-module postings with reason, correction and replay actions.

The license and usage page shall show edition, licensed modules, limits and consumption, expiry and maintenance dates, state (active, warning, grace, read-only, locked), upload of a new license file, and usage statements per month.
Announcements shall let admins post banners and messages to all users, roles or companies with schedule and acknowledgement tracking. (S)

A release notes and version page shall show installed module versions, available updates (subject to maintenance entitlement), and the change log for each version, with on-premise update bundle upload and pre-checks.
Scheduled report delivery administration shall show all schedules with owners, recipients and failures.
The pack manager shall list installed packs with version, contents summary, compatibility, overrides detected, and available updates with release notes.

Pack installation and upgrade shall show a preview of added, changed and conflicting items; conflicts shall be resolved item by item (keep tenant version, take pack version, merge), and the result applied through maker-checker.

The package manager shall export selected configuration objects (or everything) as a package with dependency detection, import packages with validation, and show diffs against the current environment.
Promotion between environments shall run validation and automated tests, take a rollback snapshot, apply after approval, and show a result report.
Rollback shall restore the snapshot of configuration without touching transactional documents, with a report of what changed back.
Implementation partners shall be able to maintain their own template packs and apply them to tenants they are authorized for. (S)
AI settings shall switch AI on or off per tenant, module, user group and skill, and show which skills are available under the entitlement.
Data policy shall define which data classes may be sent to an external provider, which provider and region apply, whether a local model is used, and whether retrieval over documents is enabled.
The interaction log shall show AI conversations and tool calls with user, skill, inputs, outputs, confirmations, outcomes and token use, with filters and export.
Usage and limits shall show tokens and calls by module and month against the entitlement, with alerts.
The configuration assistant shall be accessible from every designer, producing drafts that appear as proposed changes with diff and sandbox test, never applied directly.
Admins shall be able to disable AI for specific sensitive modules or fields (for example payroll data) regardless of user group.
A feedback mechanism shall let users rate AI responses, flag problems, and route flagged items to admins.
The tenant list shall show name, status, region, cluster, edition, modules, users, storage, license state, version, last activity and health, with filters and export.

A provisioning wizard shall create a tenant from a template: details, region and cluster selection, modules and packs, entitlement, domain, administrator, and smoke test result, with progress and failure recovery.

Entitlement management shall create and edit entitlements (editions, modules, limits, term, maintenance expiry, add-ons) with history, effective dates and approval, and link to license issuance for on-premise customers.

The license issuer (offline tool) shall produce signed license files from an entitlement, record issued licenses, and support revocation lists and re-issue; the console shall display issued licenses without holding private keys.

The fleet dashboard shall show module versions per tenant, pending migrations, migration runs with canaries and results, failed tenants in maintenance, and the ability to retry or roll back per tenant.
The pack catalog shall publish signed packs, manage versions and compatibility, and show which tenants run which pack versions.
Usage and billing support shall show monthly meters per tenant (users, employees, companies, storage, API calls, AI tokens), produce usage statements, and export to a billing system.
Health and capacity views shall show cluster capacity, database sizes, slow tenants, queue backlogs, and alerts, with tenant move planning.

Support tools shall request tenant support grants, show active grants, and open a time-boxed, scoped view of tenant configuration or data only while a grant is active, with all actions in the platform and tenant audit logs.
Platform users and roles shall be managed with MFA mandatory, separation of duties between provisioning, licensing and support roles, and a complete platform audit.
Tenant lifecycle actions (suspend, resume, move, export, offboard, delete) shall be available with approvals, legal-hold checks and retention windows.
For on-premise installs, a reduced console shall show license state, upload of new license, installed versions, update bundle application, health, and diagnostic bundle export.
Every list and designer shall be usable by keyboard, meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and screen-reader labeling, and support right-to-left languages.
Destructive and wide-impact actions shall require confirmation that states the impact (counts of affected users or records) and offer undo where technically possible.
Empty states shall explain what the area is for and offer the next action or an import option.
Error messages shall say what happened, why, and how to fix it, with a correlation id for support.
Long forms shall autosave drafts and warn before losing changes.
Admin screens shall work on tablets; critical admin approvals and monitoring shall work on phones.
Help shall be contextual, searchable, and available in the three launch languages, and shall include guided tours for first-time administrators.
Large lists shall load progressively (virtualization and server-side paging) and keep responsiveness within the targets of document 2, GR-01.

The portal administration area shall manage portal types and realms, branding and custom domains, languages, invitations and self-registration approval, external users and their partner links, inactivity expiry and access reviews, and show portal usage against the portal.external\_users entitlement (kernel PRT).
Partner administrators shall have a reduced console to manage their own external users within limits set by the tenant.

The device management area shall list registered devices with user, platform, app version and last sync, allow lock, wipe and removal, enforce minimum app versions and per-user device limits, and show sync health, backlog and conflicts (kernel SYN).
Sync scope administration shall let administrators configure what each role may hold offline, size limits and refresh policies per module.
Search administration shall show index status per entity type, allow rebuilds, manage excluded fields and synonyms, and test search as a chosen role (kernel SRC).
Collaboration settings shall configure which record types allow comments and tasks, mention and email-reply behavior, retention and legal hold (kernel COL).

Printer administration shall register printers and print agents per location and type, assign routing by document type, monitor queues, retry failed jobs and review print logs (kernel DOC-09 to DOC-11).

Administration of the semantic model, certification queue, schedules, refresh jobs, data quality results, export approvals, AI skills, provider routing, quotas and the kill switch shall be provided as specified in document 9, sections 21 (ADM) and 10 (GOV), and shall appear in the Operations and AI controls sections of the console.

Atomic posting (D-31). A document with financial effect shall complete and create its ledger entry in one database transaction through the Finance posting contract. If posting is refused, the document shall remain in its previous state and the user shall see the reason and the fix.

Operation without Finance. Where Finance is not licensed, the posting contract shall be satisfied by a kernel stub that records an accounting event for later export. No module shall test whether Finance is present.

Deferred posting by policy. Where a source is configured for deferred posting, failed postings shall enter the exception queue with an owner and an age; items older than a configured limit shall alert; a period shall not close while the queue holds items dated in it.

One source, one entry, traceable both ways. Every ledger entry shall carry the type and identifier of its source document, and every source document shall show its entries. Re-processing the same source shall never create a second entry (idempotency by source key).
Posted means immutable. A posted document shall never be edited or deleted. Correction is by reversal (a full counter-entry linked to the original) followed, if needed, by a new document.

Cancellation versus reversal. A document not yet posted may be cancelled and keeps its number with status cancelled. A posted document may only be reversed. Legal document numbers shall never be reused.

Reversal date. A reversal shall be dated in the original period if that period is open, otherwise on the first day of the earliest open period, with the original date kept for reference. Posting into a closed period shall require reopening by an authorized role, with reason, and shall be audited.

Reversal order. A document shall not be reversed while a later document depends on it. The system shall name the blocking documents and offer the correct order (for example: unmatch invoice, then reverse receipt).
Receipt before invoice. A goods receipt shall debit stock or expense and credit a goods-received-not-invoiced account at order price. Matching the supplier invoice clears that account.

Invoice before receipt. An invoice arriving first shall be held unmatched or, by policy, posted to an invoice-received-not-delivered account. It shall not be payable past a configured tolerance without a receipt, unless an authorized override with reason is recorded.

Price and quantity variance. A difference between invoice and order price within tolerance shall post to inventory (average and FIFO costing, if stock remains) or to price variance (standard costing, or stock already consumed). Outside tolerance, the invoice shall be blocked for approval.

Reversing a receipt after invoice. A receipt matched to an invoice shall not be reversed directly. The route is a supplier return document, which reduces stock at the original receipt cost and raises an expected credit note; the credit note clears it.

Partial chains. Requisition, order, receipt, invoice and payment shall each allow partial fulfilment with open quantity and open amount tracked per line. A line shall close by full fulfilment or by an explicit short-close with reason; short-closing shall release any remaining budget commitment.

Amending an approved order. A change to price, quantity, supplier, terms or delivery beyond tolerance shall create a new version, require re-approval of the difference, keep the earlier version readable, and shall not go below quantities already received or invoiced.
Return after payment. Returning goods already paid for shall create a supplier debit balance, settled by refund or offset against later invoices; it shall not reopen the paid invoice.

Landed cost after receipt. Late freight, duty or handling shall be allocated to the receipt; the share for stock still on hand adjusts inventory value, the share for stock already issued posts to cost of goods sold or variance.

Backdated stock movements. A movement dated before later movements of the same item shall be allowed only inside an open inventory period and shall trigger cost recalculation for affected later movements, posting the difference as a dated adjustment. Movements into a closed inventory period shall be refused.

Negative stock. Negative stock shall be refused by default. Where policy allows it for an item or warehouse, issues shall be costed at last known cost and corrected automatically when the covering receipt is posted.

Transfers. A transfer between warehouses of one legal entity shall move stock through an in-transit location with no profit and no revenue. A transfer between legal entities shall be an intercompany sale and purchase at the transfer price, with matching receivable and payable and elimination data for consolidation.

Reservations. Stock reserved for an order shall not be issued to another document without an explicit release. Reservations shall expire by policy and shall be released on cancellation or short-close.
Count adjustments. Stock count differences above a value threshold shall require approval before posting, and shall post to a dedicated gain or loss account with the count as source.

Partial delivery and credit hold. Sales orders shall allow partial delivery and partial invoicing per line. A customer over credit limit or with overdue balances shall be held at order confirmation and again at delivery; release shall require an authorized role and a reason.

Customer returns. A return shall reference the original invoice where known, bring stock back at the original issue cost, and raise a credit note. After payment, the credit shall be refundable or offset.

Capitalization. An asset bought through a purchase order shall be received into an asset-under-construction or clearing account and capitalized by an explicit step that creates the asset record; receipt alone shall not start depreciation. Returning it before capitalization follows FR-XM-12; after capitalization it is a disposal.

Depreciation and corrections. Depreciation shall run once per asset per period. A change to cost, life or method shall apply prospectively by default; a retrospective change shall post a catch-up entry in the current open period, never into closed periods. Transfer of an asset between cost centres or legal entities shall split depreciation by date.

Attendance lock. Attendance and leave for a pay period shall be locked when payroll is calculated. A later change shall be accepted only as a retroactive adjustment carried into the next open payroll, never by editing the locked period.

Payroll posting and reversal. An approved payroll shall post one summarized entry per legal entity and cost allocation, with employee-level detail kept in payroll. A single payslip shall be reversible before payment; after payment, correction is by adjustment in a later run or an off-cycle run.

One person, several roles. An employee who is also paid as a supplier or buys as a customer shall be one party record with several roles. Expense claims, advances and loans shall settle through the employee's payable or receivable, and payroll deductions shall reference them.

Separation with open items. Final settlement shall not complete while the employee holds open advances, loans, unreturned assets, unsubmitted expense claims, open tasks requiring handover or pending approvals in their queue. Each shall be recovered, written off with approval, or reassigned.

Transfer between legal entities. Moving an employee to another legal entity shall end the first employment and start a second, linked, with service continuity, leave balances and loan balances carried by explicit rule, and cost charged to each entity by date.

Budget commitment life cycle. Where budget control is on: requisition creates a pre-commitment, order converts it to a commitment, receipt or invoice converts it to actual, and cancellation or short-close releases it. A check that fails shall block or warn by policy; an override shall require a named role and reason. Changing a cost centre on an open document shall move its commitment.

Approvals, delegation and exceptions. An approval request shall escalate after its time limit to the next level and shall never auto-approve. Delegation shall be time-bound and recorded. Nobody shall approve their own document. Any use of an override permission (closed-period posting, credit release, tolerance override, budget override, negative stock) shall appear on a single audit exception report per period.
